lessons.title: The Nervous System and the Brain
lessons.notes_html:
The Nervous System

The nervous system controls the work of all the systems and organs of the body and creates coordination among them. It is made of a network of neurons.

  • Sensory nerves carry messages from the different parts of the body to the brain and the spinal cord.
  • The brain decides on these messages.
  • Motor nerves carry the brain's orders to the organs.

Parts of the Nervous System

PartWork
BrainThinking, understanding, deciding and controlling all actions
Spinal cordPath for messages between the brain and the body; centre of automatic (reflex) actions
NervesCarry messages to the brain and orders to the organs

According to the book, the central nervous system consists of the brain and the spinal cord, with the nerves connected to them.

The Brain

  • The brain stays protected inside the cranium (skull) — the upper part of the bone.
  • The fore-brain (cerebrum) is the largest part of the brain. It consists of two hemispheres.
  • The hind-brain has three parts: the medulla oblongata, the pons and the cerebellum.
  • Cerebellum means "little brain". It controls the balance and movement of the body.
  • The spinal cord is the extension of the brain up to the backbone.

Why the Brain is the Ruler of the Body

The brain controls the work of all the organs and systems, receives messages from the senses, decides on them and gives orders. It works all the time — even during sleep, breathing, the beating of the heart and the control of body temperature continue, so the brain never stops.

Think: Like a computer, the brain receives information, stores it and acts on it. The difference is that the brain can itself think and decide, whereas a computer only acts on the instructions given to it.

mcqs.q: The nervous system is a net or network of ___.
mcqs.why: The nervous system consists of a network of neurons. These neurons carry messages between the brain and the body, so the whole system works like a net of nerve cells.

mcqs.q: The upper part of the bone, which protects the brain, is called the ___.
mcqs.why: The cranium (skull) is the upper part of the bone. The brain stays protected inside the cranium, safe from injury.

mcqs.q: The largest part of the brain is the ___.
mcqs.why: The fore-brain, called the cerebrum, is the largest part of the brain. It consists of two hemispheres and is the upper part of the brain.

mcqs.q: Cerebellum means ___.
mcqs.why: Cerebellum means 'little brain'. It is a part of the hind-brain and controls the balance and movement of the body.

mcqs.q: The hind-brain consists of the pons and the ___.
mcqs.why: The hind-brain has three parts: the medulla oblongata, the pons and the cerebellum. Breathing and the beating of the heart are controlled from here.

mcqs.q: The extension of the brain up to the backbone is called the ___.
mcqs.why: The spinal cord extends from the brain downwards through the backbone. It is the path for messages between the brain and the body.

mcqs.q: Which of these carries messages from the body parts to the brain?
mcqs.why: Sensory nerves carry messages from the different parts of the body to the brain and the spinal cord. After the brain decides, motor nerves carry its orders to the organs.

mcqs.q: According to the book, the central nervous system is made of ___.
options: The brain, spinal cord and nerves
mcqs.why: According to the book, the central nervous system consists of the brain and the spinal cord, with the nerves connected to them.

mcqs.q: The work of the spinal cord in the nervous system is to ___.
options: Carry messages between the brain and the body
mcqs.why: The spinal cord is the path for messages between the brain and the body. It is also the centre of automatic actions, that is, reflex actions.

mcqs.q: Why does the brain work all the time, even during sleep?
options: Because breathing, heartbeat and temperature control must continue
Because the nerves rest in the day
Because the spinal cord stops working
mcqs.why: Even during sleep the necessary actions of the body continue, like breathing, the beating of the heart and the control of the body's temperature. If the brain stopped working, these actions would stop too.

mcqs.q: Thinking and emotions are controlled by the ___.
mcqs.why: Thinking and emotions are the work of the fore-brain (cerebrum). The medulla oblongata controls breathing and heartbeat, while the hypothalamus controls temperature, hunger and thirst.

mcqs.q: Breathing and the beating of the heart are controlled by the ___.
mcqs.why: Breathing and the beating of the heart are controlled by the medulla oblongata, which is a part of the hind-brain. These actions continue automatically without our will.

mcqs.q: The control of the body's temperature, hunger and thirst is the work of the ___.
mcqs.why: The hypothalamus controls the body's temperature, hunger and thirst. It keeps the inside conditions of the body balanced.

mcqs.q: Which list shows actions controlled by the nervous system?
options: Thinking, remembering, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing and digestion
Only the beating of the heart
Growing of hair and nails only
mcqs.why: The nervous system controls thinking, remembering, seeing, hearing, speaking, walking, breathing, the beating of the heart, the digestion of food and the control of temperature — almost every action of the body.

mcqs.q: How is the brain different from a computer?
options: A computer can think by itself
The brain can itself think and decide; a computer only follows given instructions
mcqs.why: Like a computer, the brain receives information, stores it and acts on it. The difference is that the brain can itself think and decide, whereas a computer only acts on the instructions given to it.

lessons.title: Lobes of the Brain, Voluntary Actions and Reflex Actions
lessons.notes_html:
The Four Lobes of the Brain

LobeWork
Frontal lobeProducing movement, intelligence, skill, speaking, reasoning, deciding and personality
Parietal lobeTranslating the stages of the senses, language, mathematics, help in reading and writing
Temporal lobeDistinguishing hearing- and memory-related information and storing it as memory
Occipital lobeSeeing and recognising the things seen

Voluntary and Involuntary Actions

Voluntary actionInvoluntary action
Done by a person's own willHappens automatically, without a person's will
Examples: walking, eating, speakingExamples: beating of the heart, breathing, digestion of food
Centre: fore-brainCentre: hind-brain

Reflex Actions

A reflex action is a quick, automatic action. Its centre is the spinal cord. Examples from daily life:

  • The hand pulling back at once when it touches a hot thing.
  • The eye blinking when something falls into it.
  • Sneezing when there is irritation or dust in the nose.
  • Coughing when food gets stuck in the throat.
  • The leg moving forward automatically when there is a light tap below the knee.

mcqs.q: Speaking, reasoning, deciding and personality are the work of the ___.
mcqs.why: The frontal lobe produces movement, intelligence, skill, speaking, reasoning, deciding and personality. It is the front part of the cerebrum.

mcqs.q: The lobe that helps in reading, writing, language and mathematics is the ___.
mcqs.why: The parietal lobe translates the stages of the senses and deals with language and mathematics. It also helps in reading and writing.

mcqs.q: Hearing and memory are looked after by the ___.
mcqs.why: The temporal lobe distinguishes hearing- and memory-related information and stores it as memory. That is why we remember sounds and voices.

mcqs.q: Seeing and recognising the things seen is the work of the ___.
mcqs.why: The occipital lobe does the work of seeing and recognising the things seen. It is present at the back of the brain.

mcqs.q: Walking, eating and speaking are examples of ___.
mcqs.why: These actions are done by a person's own will, so they are voluntary actions. Their centre is the fore-brain.

mcqs.q: The beating of the heart and the digestion of food are ___.
mcqs.why: These actions happen automatically without a person's will, so they are involuntary actions. Their centre is the hind-brain.

mcqs.q: The centre of voluntary actions is the ___.
mcqs.why: Voluntary actions are done by our own will and their centre is the fore-brain. Involuntary actions, on the other hand, are centred in the hind-brain.

mcqs.q: When a hand touches a hot thing and pulls back at once, this is a ___.
mcqs.why: Pulling the hand back at once from a hot thing is a reflex action. Sneezing, coughing and blinking of the eye are also reflex actions of daily life.

mcqs.q: The centre of reflex (automatic) actions is the ___.
mcqs.why: The spinal cord is the centre of automatic actions (reflex actions). Because the message does not need to travel to the brain first, the action is very quick.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a reflex action?
options: Writing a letter to a friend
Sneezing when dust enters the nose
Blinking when something falls in the eye
Coughing when food sticks in the throat
mcqs.why: Writing a letter is a voluntary action done by our own will and thinking. Sneezing, blinking and coughing happen automatically, so they are reflex actions.

lessons.title: The Excretory System and the Kidney
lessons.notes_html:
Why the Body Needs an Excretory System

During the processes of eating and breathing, waste materials are produced in the body: urea, carbon dioxide, extra water and salts. If these do not leave the body, they become poisonous and harm the body. The excretory system throws them out.

  • The waste obtained during the breathing process of the cell is carbon dioxide.
  • Through sweat, extra water, salts and other waste materials also leave the body — so the skin also helps in excretion, and sweating keeps the body cool during exercise.

The Kidney — the Main Organ

  • The kidney cleans the blood, separates waste materials like urea, extra water and salts from it and makes urine.
  • It keeps the quantity of water in the body in balance. Without the kidney, waste materials would collect in the blood and make the body poisonous.
  • Parts of the excretory system (for the diagram): two kidneys, arteries and veins of the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra.

When a Kidney Fails

  • Dialysis machine — the artificial kidney machine. When a kidney fails, it removes waste materials from the blood.
  • Kidney transplant — a completely failed kidney is managed by removing the damaged kidney and fitting a healthy kidney in its place.
  • Common kidney diseases: kidney stones, infection, and kidney failure caused by diabetes and high blood pressure.
  • The liver also helps in separating waste materials from the blood, and its work is connected with the kidney — so a doctor may also advise a liver function check.
  • A person born with one kidney can live normally, but should drink plenty of water, avoid excessive salt and medicines, keep blood pressure and sugar under control, and get checked by a doctor from time to time.

mcqs.q: The main organ of the excretory process is the ___.
mcqs.why: The kidney is the main organ of the excretory system. It cleans the blood and removes waste materials in the form of urine.

mcqs.q: The waste thing obtained during the breathing process of the cell is ___.
mcqs.why: Carbon dioxide is the waste material produced during the breathing process of the cell. It is removed from the body through the lungs.

mcqs.q: The artificial kidney machine is called the ___.
mcqs.why: The dialysis machine is called the artificial kidney. When a kidney fails, this machine does the work of removing waste materials from the blood.

mcqs.q: A completely failed kidney can be managed through ___.
mcqs.why: A completely failed kidney is managed through kidney transplant: the damaged kidney is removed and a healthy kidney is fitted in its place.

mcqs.q: Changing a damaged kidney into a healthy kidney is called ___.
mcqs.why: Fitting a healthy kidney in place of a damaged kidney is called transplantation. It is different from transpiration, which is a process in plants.

mcqs.q: Which is the main organ of the urine excretion process?
mcqs.why: The kidney is the main organ of urine excretion. It separates urea, extra water and salts from the blood and makes urine.

mcqs.q: Why does the body need the excretory system?
options: To throw out waste materials that would otherwise poison the body
mcqs.why: During eating and breathing, waste materials (urea, carbon dioxide, extra water and salts) are produced. If these do not leave the body, they become poisonous, so the excretory system must throw them out.

mcqs.q: The kidney keeps which of these in balance in the body?
mcqs.why: The kidney cleans the blood, makes urine and keeps the quantity of water in the body in balance. Without it, waste would collect in the blood and poison the body.

mcqs.q: Which parts are shown in a labelled diagram of the human excretory system?
options: Two kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra
mcqs.why: The excretory system diagram shows the two kidneys, the arteries and veins of the kidneys, the ureters, the bladder and the urethra, each with its label.

mcqs.q: During exercise people sweat a lot. Besides keeping the body cool, sweating also ___.
options: Removes extra water, salts and waste materials from the body
mcqs.why: Through sweat, extra water and salts and other waste materials also leave the body. In this way the skin also helps in the excretory process.

mcqs.q: A person born with one kidney should take which precaution?
options: Drink plenty of water and keep blood pressure and sugar under control
mcqs.why: Such a person should protect the one kidney: drink plenty of water, avoid excessive use of salt and medicines, keep blood pressure and sugar under control, and get checked by a doctor from time to time.

mcqs.q: Common diseases of the kidney include ___.
options: Kidney stones, infection and failure from diabetes and high blood pressure
mcqs.why: The common diseases of the kidney are kidney stones, infection, and kidney failure caused by diabetes and high blood pressure. This is why sugar and blood pressure must be controlled.

mcqs.q: Why does a doctor often advise a liver function check for kidney-problem patients?
options: The liver also separates waste from the blood and its work is connected with the kidney
The liver is a part of the kidney
mcqs.why: The liver also plays an important role in separating waste materials from the blood and cleaning the body. A fault in the liver can produce symptoms like those of kidney problems.

mcqs.q: In the dialysis process, the machine removes ___ from the blood.
mcqs.why: The dialysis machine removes waste materials from the blood of a kidney patient, doing the work of the failed kidney outside the body.

mcqs.q: Urea, extra water and salts are separated from the blood by the ___.
mcqs.why: The kidneys separate waste materials like urea, extra water and salts from the blood and make urine from them. This keeps the blood clean.

lessons.title: Cell Division — Mitosis and Meiosis
lessons.notes_html:
Cell Division

Cell division is the general process in which both the nucleus and the cytoplasm divide. There are two ways of cell division:

MitosisMeiosis
Takes place inBody cellsSex cells
Number of divisionsOne divisionTwo divisions (I and II)
Cells formedTwo cellsFour cells
ChromosomesNumber stays the sameNumber becomes half
New cellsLike the parent cellDifferent from the parent cell
PurposeGrowth and repair of the bodyMaking sex cells (gametes); keeping the chromosome number maintained

Important Terms

  • Mitosis — division of the nucleus in which two identical nuclei are formed from one nucleus; after that, in cytokinesis, the cytoplasm divides and two new cells are formed.
  • Meiosis — reduction division; the number of chromosomes becomes half and four cells are formed from one cell.
  • Interphase — the stage in which the cell prepares for division: the DNA is copied (replication), the cell grows, and the materials needed for division are prepared.
  • Cytokinesis — the division of the cytoplasm in cell division, by which two separate cells are formed.
  • Prophase — the first stage of mitosis, in which the chromosomes appear.
  • Haploid (n) — one set of chromosomes, as in the sex cells (gametes). Diploid (2n) — two sets of chromosomes, as in the ordinary body cells.

Project in the book: make a Mitosis Flip Book — draw the stages in order (interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis) on cards; flipping the pages quickly shows the cell dividing.

mcqs.q: The two ways of cell division are ___.
mcqs.why: There are two ways of cell division: mitosis, which takes place in body cells for growth and repair, and meiosis, which takes place in sex cells to make gametes.

mcqs.q: Meiosis is called reduction division because ___.
options: The number of chromosomes becomes half
mcqs.why: In meiosis the number of chromosomes becomes half, so it is called reduction division. Four cells are formed from one cell by two divisions.

mcqs.q: In mitosis, the number of cells formed from one cell is ___.
mcqs.why: In mitosis there is one division and two cells are formed. The new cells are like the parent cell and the chromosome number stays the same.

mcqs.q: The purpose of interphase is that ___.
options: The cell prepares for division — DNA is copied and the cell grows
mcqs.why: In interphase the cell prepares for division: the DNA is copied (replication), the cell grows, and the materials needed for division are prepared.

mcqs.q: The division of the cytoplasm in cell division is called ___.
mcqs.why: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, by which two separate cells are formed. It happens after the nucleus has divided in mitosis.

mcqs.q: Haploid (n) means ___.
mcqs.why: Haploid (n) means one set of chromosomes, as in the sex cells (gametes). Diploid (2n) means two sets of chromosomes, as in the ordinary body cells.

mcqs.q: Meiosis takes place in ___.
mcqs.why: Meiosis takes place in sex cells and makes gametes. Mitosis, in contrast, takes place in body cells for growth and repair.

mcqs.q: Prophase is ___.
options: The first stage of mitosis, in which the chromosomes appear
mcqs.why: Prophase is the first stage of mitosis, in which the chromosomes appear. The stages continue as metaphase, anaphase and telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

mcqs.q: In meiosis, the number of divisions and cells formed is ___.
mcqs.why: In meiosis there are two divisions (meiosis I and II) and four cells are formed from one cell. In mitosis there is only one division and two cells are formed.

mcqs.q: The purpose of mitosis is ___.
options: Growth and repair of the body
mcqs.why: Mitosis divides the body cells; its purpose is the growth and repair of the body. The cells formed are like the parent cell.

mcqs.q: Cell division is different from mitosis because ___.
options: Cell division happens only in plants
Cell division is the general process of nucleus and cytoplasm dividing; mitosis is the division of the nucleus only
mcqs.why: Cell division is the general process in which both the nucleus and the cytoplasm divide. Mitosis is the division of the nucleus in which two identical nuclei are formed; cytokinesis then divides the cytoplasm.

mcqs.q: In a Mitosis Flip Book, the stages are drawn in which order?
options: Interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis
mcqs.why: The stages of mitosis in order are: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase and cytokinesis. Flipping the cards quickly makes the division of the cell appear to move.

mcqs.q: The cells formed by meiosis are ___ the parent cell.
mcqs.why: The cells formed by meiosis are different from the parent cell and have half the number of chromosomes. The cells formed by mitosis are like the parent cell.

mcqs.q: Replication of DNA takes place during ___.
mcqs.why: In interphase the cell prepares for division and the DNA is copied — this copying is called replication. The cell also grows in this stage.

mcqs.q: Diploid (2n) cells are found in ___.
mcqs.why: Diploid (2n) means two sets of chromosomes, as in the ordinary body cells. The sex cells (gametes) are haploid, with one set.

lessons.title: Heredity, Chromosomes and DNA
lessons.notes_html:
Heredity

Heredity is the transfer of characteristics or traits from parents to offspring — the way by which the characteristics of the parents are transferred to the children.

Examples of hereditary characteristics: the colour of the eyes, the colour and texture of the hair, height, the ability to roll the tongue, and whether the ear lobe is attached or free. Such characteristics are received from the parents through the genes in inheritance.

Chromosomes, Genes and DNA

  • Chromosomes contain DNA; they are made of DNA and protein.
  • Homologous chromosomes — the pair of chromosomes in which one chromosome comes from the father and one from the mother, and both are alike in shape, size and genes.
  • Gene — the part of the DNA which carries the information of one hereditary characteristic.
  • DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) — the material which carries hereditary information. It is present in the chromosomes in the nucleus, is like a two-stranded ladder (double helix), and is made of nucleotides; each nucleotide contains sugar, phosphate and a nitrogen base (adenine, thymine, guanine or cytosine).

mcqs.q: The transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring is called ___.
mcqs.why: Heredity is the way by which the characteristics of the parents are transferred to the offspring, for example eye colour, hair colour and height.

mcqs.q: Chromosomes contain ___.
mcqs.why: Chromosomes contain DNA. They are made of DNA and protein, and the DNA carries the hereditary information.

mcqs.q: Characteristics like rolling the tongue and the ear lobe are received from the parents ___.
mcqs.why: These characteristics are transferred from parents to offspring through the information present in the genes. They are hereditary characteristics.

mcqs.q: A gene is ___.
options: The part of DNA carrying information of one hereditary characteristic
A kind of protein in food
mcqs.why: A gene is the part of the DNA which carries the information of one hereditary characteristic, such as the colour of the eyes.

mcqs.q: Homologous chromosomes are ___.
options: A pair in which one comes from the father and one from the mother, alike in shape, size and genes
mcqs.why: Homologous chromosomes are the pair in which one chromosome comes from the father and one from the mother. Both are alike in shape, size and genes.

mcqs.q: DNA is present in the ___ of the cell.
mcqs.why: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is the material which carries hereditary information. It is present in the chromosomes in the nucleus of the cell.

mcqs.q: The shape of DNA is like a ___.
mcqs.why: DNA is like a two-stranded ladder, called the double helix. It is made of nucleotides joined in two twisted strands.

mcqs.q: Each nucleotide of DNA contains ___.
options: Sugar, phosphate and a nitrogen base
mcqs.why: Each nucleotide contains sugar, phosphate and a nitrogen base. The nitrogen bases are adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a hereditary characteristic?
mcqs.why: The colour of the eyes is a hereditary characteristic received from the parents through genes. Hair colour and texture, height, tongue rolling and ear lobe type are also hereditary.

mcqs.q: Whether the ear lobe is attached or free is decided by ___.
mcqs.why: Ear lobe type is a hereditary characteristic. Like tongue rolling, it is transferred from parents to offspring through the information present in the genes.

lessons.title: What is Biotechnology?
lessons.notes_html:
What is Biotechnology?

Biotechnology is the scientific knowledge in which living organisms or their materials are used with technology in an ethical way to produce useful things or solutions to problems.

Role of Bacteria

Bacteria are used in genetic engineering: a foreign gene is inserted into their plasmid, and the bacteria produce human insulin, proteins and other things from that gene in large quantity.

Products and Uses in Daily Life

  • Insulin for diabetes.
  • Vaccines for protection from diseases (BCG, measles, polio, hepatitis).
  • Growth hormone for the treatment of dwarfism.
  • Preparation of cheese, yoghurt and bread made with yeast.
  • Genetically changed crops (maize, wheat, rice, cotton, soybean) and crops with more nutrition, like rice with vitamin A.
  • Bananas prepared through tissue culture.

mcqs.q: Biotechnology is the use of ___ to produce useful things.
options: Living organisms or their materials with technology
mcqs.why: Biotechnology is the scientific knowledge in which living organisms or their materials are used with technology in an ethical way to produce useful things or solutions to problems.

mcqs.q: In genetic engineering, a foreign gene is inserted into the ___ of bacteria.
mcqs.why: A foreign gene is inserted into the plasmid of bacteria. The bacteria then produce human insulin, proteins and other things from that gene in large quantity.

mcqs.q: Human insulin for diabetes patients is prepared on a commercial scale using ___.
mcqs.why: The gene of human insulin is inserted into the plasmid of bacteria, and insulin is prepared in large quantity through the bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a product of biotechnology in food?
options: Cheese and yoghurt made with microbes and yeast
mcqs.why: Cheese, yoghurt and bread made with yeast are food products of biotechnology. Genetically changed crops and tissue-culture bananas are its agriculture products.

mcqs.q: Bananas are prepared in large numbers through ___.
mcqs.why: Bananas are prepared through tissue culture, a biotechnology method. Many identical plants are produced quickly by this method.

mcqs.q: Vaccines prepared by biotechnology protect us from diseases like ___.
mcqs.why: Vaccines for protection from diseases — BCG, measles, polio, hepatitis — are an important daily-life use of biotechnology.

mcqs.q: Genetically changed crops mentioned in the book include ___.
options: Maize, wheat, rice, cotton and soybean
mcqs.why: Examples of products prepared in food and agriculture with biotechnology are genetically changed crops: maize, wheat, rice, cotton and soybean.

mcqs.q: Rice rich in vitamin A is prepared by ___.
options: Inserting the gene of vitamin A into the rice plant
mcqs.why: The gene of vitamin A is inserted into the rice plant to make it rich in vitamin A. Such crops with more nutrition are a product of biotechnology.

mcqs.q: The human growth hormone product is used for the treatment of ___.
mcqs.why: The product of the human growth hormone is used for the treatment of dwarfism. Insulin, in contrast, is used for diabetes.

mcqs.q: Biotechnology uses living organisms in which way?
mcqs.why: By definition, biotechnology uses living organisms or their materials with technology in an ethical way to produce useful things or solutions to problems.

lessons.title: DNA, Genes and Biotechnology Products
lessons.notes_html:
DNA — the Coded Information

  • In DNA, information is kept in the form of coded writing. It has 4 organic bases: adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine.
  • Uracil is NOT a base of DNA — it is a base of RNA.
  • Watson and Crick proposed the model of DNA in 1953 — the double-helix structure.
  • Replication — the stage of the copying of DNA is called replication.
  • Plasmid — the small pieces (small circular pieces) of DNA present in bacteria, which can be copied.

Vaccines and Antibodies

  • A vaccine contains weak or dead microbes (pathogens); it weakens the disease-spreading organisms' effect by making antibodies in the body, and protects from disease.
  • Measles is a disease that can be treated/protected against through the use of a vaccine.

Matching (from the book)

Column AColumn B
DNADouble-helix structure
ReplicationCopies
Separation of insulinHuman pancreas

mcqs.q: The stage of the copying of DNA is called ___.
mcqs.why: The stage of the copying of DNA is called replication. Copies of DNA are formed by replication before the cell divides.

mcqs.q: DNA has how many organic bases?
mcqs.why: DNA has four organic bases: adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine. In DNA, information is kept in the form of this coded writing.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT an organic base of DNA?
mcqs.why: Uracil is a base of RNA, not of DNA. The bases of DNA are adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine.

mcqs.q: The small circular pieces of DNA in bacteria are called ___.
mcqs.why: A plasmid is a small circular piece of DNA present in bacteria which can be copied. Foreign genes are inserted into plasmids in genetic engineering.

mcqs.q: The model of DNA was proposed in 1953 by ___.
mcqs.why: Watson and Crick presented the double-helix model of DNA in 1953. The model is like a ladder of two twisted strands.

mcqs.q: Which disease can be treated through the use of a vaccine?
mcqs.why: A vaccine is given for protection from measles. A vaccine contains weak or dead microbes which make antibodies in the body.

mcqs.q: A vaccine protects the body because it ___.
options: Contains weak or dead microbes which make antibodies in the body
mcqs.why: A vaccine contains weak or dead microbes (pathogens) which make antibodies in the body and protect from disease. It weakens the effect of the disease-spreading organisms.

mcqs.q: In the book's matching, DNA matches with ___.
mcqs.why: DNA matches with the double-helix structure — the model of DNA is like a ladder of two twisted strands. Replication matches with copies, and separation of insulin with the human pancreas.

mcqs.q: Insulin is naturally separated (produced) in the body by the ___.
mcqs.why: Insulin comes out of the human pancreas. In biotechnology, its gene is inserted into bacteria to prepare it in large quantity.

mcqs.q: Vitamin A gene is inserted into which plant to make it rich in vitamin A?
mcqs.why: The rice plant is genetically changed with the gene of vitamin A to obtain rice rich in vitamin A. This is an example of a crop with more nutrition.

mcqs.q: Which of these weakens the disease-spreading organisms (pathogens), as asked in the book's exercise?
mcqs.why: According to the book's exercise, the vaccine weakens the disease-spreading organisms (pathogens) — it contains weak or dead microbes that train the body to make antibodies.

mcqs.q: The structure of DNA includes ___.
mcqs.why: The structure of DNA includes sugar and organic bases (with phosphate), arranged in two twisted strands — the double helix.

chapters.title: Unit 4: Pollution and Its Effects on the Environment

lessons.title: Pollution and Air Pollutants
lessons.notes_html:
What is Pollution?

Pollution is such an unnatural change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water and land which harms the environment and the life of living things.

According to the book, air pollution is an extremely delicate and dangerous type of environmental pollution.

Main Air Pollutants

PollutantCauses / SourcesEffects
Sulphur dioxideSmoke of factories and vehicles (poisonous gas with a biting smell)Difficulty in breathing
Carbon monoxideBurning of fuelHarmful poisonous gas
Carbon dioxideComes out from the burning of fuelGreenhouse effect
Nitrogen dioxideSmoke and burning of fuelBreathing diseases
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFC)Use of refrigeratorsDestroys the ozone layer

Effects of air pollution on the human body: breathing diseases, cough, cold, headache, heart diseases, damage to the nervous system and spoiling of the lungs.

Other Points from the Book

  • Acid rain harms (destroys) historical buildings and statues.
  • The panda is included among the animals of rare species, which need to be saved.
  • Excessive use of chemical fertiliser produces pollution in land and water; the cutting of trees is deforestation.

Ways to Reduce Pollution

  • Planting more trees.
  • Reducing the use of fuel.
  • Fitting filters on the chimneys of factories.
  • Reusing and recycling things — this also saves the natural resources of the earth.
  • Reducing the use of chemical fertilisers and insect-killing medicines.
  • Not wasting water.
  • Creating awareness among people and acting on the law.

mcqs.q: Pollution is ___.
options: A natural change that helps life
An unnatural change in air, water and land which harms the environment and life
mcqs.why: Pollution is such an unnatural change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water and land which harms the environment and the life of living things.

mcqs.q: According to the book, the extremely delicate and dangerous type of pollution is ___.
mcqs.why: According to the book, air pollution is an extremely dangerous type of environmental pollution, because polluted air spreads everywhere and enters the body with every breath.

mcqs.q: The main air pollutants are ___.
options: Sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide and chlorofluorocarbon
mcqs.why: The main air pollutants are sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide and chlorofluorocarbon. Their causes are smoke from factories and vehicles, the burning of fuel, and the use of refrigerators.

mcqs.q: Air pollution causes which effects on the human body?
options: Breathing diseases, cough, cold, headache, heart diseases and damage to the lungs
mcqs.why: Air pollution causes breathing diseases, cough, cold, headache, heart diseases, damage to the nervous system and spoiling of the lungs.

mcqs.q: Which gas comes out because of the burning of fuel?
mcqs.why: Carbon dioxide gas comes out from the burning of fuel. It is also the main gas responsible for the greenhouse effect.

mcqs.q: The poisonous gas with a biting smell in the smoke of motor vehicles is ___.
mcqs.why: Sulphur dioxide is a poisonous gas which is present in the smoke of vehicles and has a biting smell. It creates difficulty in breathing.

mcqs.q: What is included in the destruction of historical buildings?
mcqs.why: Acid rain harms historical buildings and statues. It is formed when pollutant gases mix with rain water.

mcqs.q: Which process can save the natural resources of the earth?
mcqs.why: By reusing and recycling things, natural resources are saved. Planting trees, reducing fuel use and not wasting water also reduce pollution.

mcqs.q: ___ is included among the animals of rare species.
mcqs.why: The panda is an animal of a rare species which needs to be saved. Pollution and destruction of forests put such rare animals in danger.

mcqs.q: Effects like drowsiness and unclear speech occur from the effect of ___.
mcqs.why: In the book's matching exercise, drowsiness and unclear speech are given as effects of chlorofluorocarbon. CFC also destroys the ozone layer.

lessons.title: The Ozone Layer and the Greenhouse Effect
lessons.notes_html:
The Ozone Layer

  • The ozone layer is the layer which protects the earth. It protects the earth from the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun.
  • If this layer were not there, these rays would produce skin cancer and other diseases in living things.
  • The ozone layer is present in the atmosphere at a height of about 12 to 50 kilometres above the land surface.
  • The special cause of the hole in the ozone layer is chlorofluorocarbon (CFC), which destroys the ozone layer. CFC is used in refrigerators.

The Greenhouse Effect

The greenhouse effect is the process in which gases like carbon dioxide, methane and chlorofluorocarbon hold the sun's heat on the earth, by which the earth becomes warm and the global temperature rises.

  • Carbon dioxide is the gas especially responsible for the greenhouse effect.
  • Carbon dioxide comes out from the burning of fuel — so reducing fuel use also reduces the greenhouse effect.

mcqs.q: The role of the ozone layer is to ___.
options: Protect the earth from the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun
mcqs.why: The ozone layer protects the earth from the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun. If it were not there, these rays would produce skin cancer and other diseases in living things.

mcqs.q: The special cause of the hole in the ozone layer is ___.
mcqs.why: Chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) destroys the ozone layer and creates a hole in it. CFCs are used in refrigerators.

mcqs.q: The layer which protects the earth is called ___.
mcqs.why: The ozone layer protects the earth from the harmful rays of the sun. It is the earth's protective layer in the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: The ozone layer is present at a height of about ___ above the land surface.
mcqs.why: The ozone layer is at a height of 12 to 50 kilometres above the earth. It absorbs the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays in this region of the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: The greenhouse effect is the process in which ___.
options: Gases like carbon dioxide and methane hold the sun's heat on the earth
mcqs.why: In the greenhouse effect, gases like carbon dioxide, methane and chlorofluorocarbon hold the sun's heat on the earth, by which the earth becomes warm and the global temperature rises.

mcqs.q: Which gas is especially responsible for the greenhouse effect?
mcqs.why: Carbon dioxide is the main gas of the greenhouse effect. It comes out from the burning of fuel and holds the sun's heat on the earth.

mcqs.q: If the ozone layer were not there, the ultraviolet rays would cause ___.
mcqs.why: Without the ozone layer, the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun would reach the earth and produce skin cancer and other diseases in living things.

mcqs.q: Chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) is used in ___.
mcqs.why: The use of refrigerators is one of the causes of CFC release. CFC destroys the ozone layer and also takes part in the greenhouse effect.

mcqs.q: Which of these gases is a greenhouse gas?
mcqs.why: Methane is a greenhouse gas, along with carbon dioxide and chlorofluorocarbon. These gases hold the sun's heat on the earth.

mcqs.q: Cutting of trees for ever (deforestation) increases pollution because ___.
options: Trees clean the air and take in carbon dioxide
mcqs.why: Trees take in carbon dioxide and clean the air. Cutting forests (deforestation) therefore increases pollution, while planting more trees is a way to reduce it.

lessons.title: Chemical Reactions and Their Signs
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Chemical Reaction?

A chemical reaction is the process in which one or more things (reactants) change and make new things (products) with new characteristics, and the original thing is not got back.

Examples from daily life: the digestion of food, milk turning sour, rusting of iron, the burning of a matchstick, and photosynthesis.

Four Signs of a Chemical Reaction

  • Formation of a new thing with new characteristics.
  • Absorption or release of energy (heat or light).
  • Change in colour.
  • Production of gas or bubbles, or the coming of a smell.

The best sign of a chemical reaction taking place is, for example, bubbles forming when a metal is put in acidic water — the formation of gas is a clear sign.

A Reaction in an Equation

Burning of methane: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O — the products obtained are carbon dioxide and water.

Leaves changing colour in autumn is a chemical reaction, because new materials are formed in the leaves.

mcqs.q: A chemical reaction is a process in which ___.
options: Only the shape of a thing changes
A thing melts and comes back
Reactants change and make new products with new characteristics
mcqs.why: In a chemical reaction, one or more reactants change and make new products with new characteristics, and the original thing is not got back — like rusting of iron or digestion of food.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of a chemical reaction?
mcqs.why: In digestion, food breaks and makes new materials which are absorbed in the body, so it is a chemical reaction. Melting, grinding and dissolving are physical changes.

mcqs.q: The four signs that show a chemical reaction are ___.
options: New thing formed, energy absorbed or released, colour change, gas or smell produced
mcqs.why: A chemical reaction is shown by: (1) formation of a new thing with new characteristics, (2) absorption or release of energy, (3) change in colour, (4) production of gas or bubbles, or the coming of a smell.

mcqs.q: What is the best sign of a chemical reaction taking place?
options: Blue colour changing water to blue
A white thing dissolving in water
Bubbles forming when a metal is put in acidic water
mcqs.why: The formation of gas or bubbles is a clear sign of a chemical reaction. Bubbles forming when a metal is put in acidic water show that a new gas is being produced.

mcqs.q: In the reaction CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, the products obtained are ___.
mcqs.why: By the burning of methane, carbon dioxide and water are obtained. The things on the right side of the arrow are the products of the reaction.

mcqs.q: Leaves changing colour in autumn is a chemical reaction because ___.
options: New materials are formed in the leaves
mcqs.why: In the changing of the colour of leaves, new materials are formed, so this is a chemical reaction — not just a change of shape or state.

mcqs.q: In a chemical reaction, the starting things are called ___ and the new things made are called ___.
mcqs.why: The things that take part in the reaction are the reactants, and the new things formed with new characteristics are the products.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a sign of a chemical reaction?
options: Change only in size and shape
mcqs.why: A change only in size and shape is a physical change. A chemical reaction shows a new thing formed, energy absorbed or released, colour change, or gas/smell produced.

mcqs.q: Photosynthesis is a chemical reaction because ___.
options: Glucose (a new material) is formed from carbon dioxide and water
mcqs.why: In photosynthesis, carbon dioxide and water change into glucose and oxygen — new materials are formed, so it is a chemical reaction: 6CO2 + 6H2O + sunlight → C6H12O6 + 6O2.

mcqs.q: Rusting of iron is a chemical change because ___.
options: Rust is a new material formed by the combination of iron and oxygen
mcqs.why: Rust is a new material which is formed by the combination of iron and oxygen. Once rusted, the original iron is not got back, so it is a chemical change.

lessons.title: Physical and Chemical Changes
lessons.notes_html:
Physical Change and Chemical Change

In a physical change, only the size, shape or state of a thing changes; its chemical characteristics stay the same and no new material is formed. In a chemical change, new materials are formed and the thing does not come back to its original state.

ExamplePhysical (P) or Chemical (C)?Reason
A lock rustingCRust is a new material (iron + oxygen)
Melting of icePIce becomes water; the chemical characteristic of water stays the same
Milk turning sourCNew materials are formed; milk does not come back
Digestion of foodCFood breaks and makes new materials
Meat rotting in sunlightCNew smelly materials are formed
Making a design on copperPOnly the shape of the copper changes
Mixing sugar in waterPSugar dissolves; no new material is formed
Grinding a stone into powderPOnly size and shape change
Burning of a matchstickCNew materials (ash, gases) are formed; the matchstick is not got back

mcqs.q: Melting of ice is a ___ change.
mcqs.why: Melting of ice is a physical change. Ice melts and becomes water, but the chemical characteristic of water stays the same.

mcqs.q: Milk turning sour is a ___ change.
mcqs.why: Milk turning sour is a chemical change. New materials are formed in the milk and the milk does not come back to its original state.

mcqs.q: Making a design on a piece of copper is a ___ change.
mcqs.why: By making a design, the shape of the copper changes but its chemical characteristic stays the same, so it is a physical change.

mcqs.q: Grinding a stone into powder is a physical change because ___.
options: Only its size and shape change
mcqs.why: By grinding a stone into powder, only its size and shape change. No new material is formed, so it is a physical change.

mcqs.q: Burning of a matchstick is a chemical change because ___.
options: New materials (ash, gases) are formed and the matchstick is not got back
mcqs.why: By burning, new materials (ash, gases) are formed and the matchstick is not got back. This is the mark of a chemical change.

mcqs.q: Mixing sugar in water is a ___ change.
mcqs.why: Sugar dissolves in water but no new material is formed, so mixing sugar in water is a physical change.

mcqs.q: Meat kept in sunlight rotting is a chemical change because ___.
options: New smelly materials are formed and it does not come back to its original state
mcqs.why: When meat rots, new smelly materials are formed in it and the meat does not come back to its original state — a chemical change.

mcqs.q: Digestion of food is a chemical change because ___.
options: Food is chewed into small pieces
Food breaks and makes new materials which are absorbed in the body
mcqs.why: In digestion, food breaks and makes new materials which are absorbed in the body. The formation of new materials makes it a chemical change.

mcqs.q: A lock rusting is a ___ change.
mcqs.why: Rusting is a chemical change. Rust is a new material which is formed by the combination of iron and oxygen.

mcqs.q: In a physical change, the ___ of a thing stays the same.
mcqs.why: In a physical change only size, shape or state may change, but the chemical characteristics of the thing stay the same and no new material is formed.

lessons.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
lessons.notes_html:
Balancing Chemical Equations

An equation is balanced when the number of atoms of every element is the same on both sides. The book's balanced equations:

UnbalancedBalanced
S8 + O2 → SO2S8 + 8O2 → 8SO2
C2H6 + O2 → CO2 + H2O2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O
P4 + O2 → P2O5P4 + 5O2 → 2P2O5
Ag + S8 → Ag2S16Ag + S8 → 8Ag2S
Al + Br2 → AlBr32Al + 3Br2 → 2AlBr3
Cr + O2 → Cr2O34Cr + 3O2 → 2Cr2O3
NaClO3 → NaCl + O22NaClO3 → 2NaCl + 3O2
AlBr3 + Cl2 → AlCl3 + Br22AlBr3 + 3Cl2 → 2AlCl3 + 3Br2

Word Equations Written as Balanced Equations

  • Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O + sunlight → C6H12O6 + 6O2
  • Carbon monoxide and oxygen: 2CO + O2 → 2CO2
  • Zinc and hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2
  • HCl and sodium hydroxide: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O
  • Decomposition of potassium chlorate: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for S8 + O2 → SO2 is ___.
mcqs.why: S8 + 8O2 → 8SO2. There are 8 sulphur atoms on the left, so 8 molecules of SO2 are needed on the right, which need 16 oxygen atoms = 8O2.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for P4 + O2 → P2O5 is ___.
mcqs.why: P4 + 5O2 → 2P2O5. Two molecules of P2O5 contain 4 phosphorus and 10 oxygen atoms, so 5O2 is needed on the left.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for Al + Br2 → AlBr3 is ___.
mcqs.why: 2Al + 3Br2 → 2AlBr3. Two AlBr3 need 2 aluminium and 6 bromine atoms, which come from 2Al and 3Br2.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for the decomposition of NaClO3 is ___.
mcqs.why: 2NaClO3 → 2NaCl + 3O2. Two formula units of NaClO3 give 6 oxygen atoms, which make 3O2 on the right side.

mcqs.q: Zinc and hydrochloric acid react as ___.
mcqs.why: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2. Zinc chloride and hydrogen gas are formed; the bubbles of hydrogen are a sign of the reaction.

mcqs.q: Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide react as ___.
mcqs.why: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O. An acid and a base make a salt and water; the equation is already balanced.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation of photosynthesis is ___.
mcqs.why: 6CO2 + 6H2O + sunlight → C6H12O6 + 6O2. Six molecules each of carbon dioxide and water make one glucose molecule and six oxygen molecules.

mcqs.q: Carbon monoxide and oxygen react as ___.
mcqs.why: 2CO + O2 → 2CO2. Two molecules of carbon monoxide take one molecule of oxygen to make two molecules of carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for Ag + S8 → Ag2S is ___.
mcqs.why: 16Ag + S8 → 8Ag2S. Eight molecules of Ag2S need 16 silver atoms and 8 sulphur atoms, and S8 already has 8 sulphur atoms.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for Cr + O2 → Cr2O3 is ___.
mcqs.why: 4Cr + 3O2 → 2Cr2O3. Two molecules of Cr2O3 contain 4 chromium and 6 oxygen atoms, so 4Cr and 3O2 are needed.

mcqs.q: The decomposition of potassium chlorate is written as ___.
mcqs.why: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2. On heating, potassium chlorate decomposes into potassium chloride and oxygen gas.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for C2H6 + O2 → CO2 + H2O is ___.
mcqs.why: 2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O. Two molecules of ethane give 4 carbon and 12 hydrogen atoms, needing 14 oxygen atoms = 7O2.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for AlBr3 + Cl2 → AlCl3 + Br2 is ___.
mcqs.why: 2AlBr3 + 3Cl2 → 2AlCl3 + 3Br2. The 6 bromine atoms on the left make 3Br2, and the 6 chlorine atoms from 3Cl2 make 2AlCl3.

mcqs.q: An equation is balanced when ___.
options: Both sides look equal in length
The number of atoms of every element is the same on both sides
mcqs.why: An equation is balanced when the number of atoms of every element is equal on the left side (reactants) and the right side (products). We change only the big numbers (coefficients), never the small numbers in the formulas.

mcqs.q: In the balanced equation 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, the products are ___.
mcqs.why: The product is water (2H2O). Hydrogen and oxygen are the reactants on the left side of the arrow.

lessons.title: Types of Chemical Reactions — Exothermic, Endothermic, Addition and Decomposition
lessons.notes_html:
Exothermic and Endothermic Processes

Exothermic processEndothermic process
Heat comes out (is released)Heat is absorbed
Examples: burning of fuel, breathing (respiration)Examples: decomposition of mercury oxide, photosynthesis
2H2 + O2 → 2H2O + heat2HgO + heat → 2Hg + O2

Importance of exothermic processes: they give us heat and energy — the burning of fuel gives heat for cooking food, warming houses and running engines; from breathing (respiration) the body gets energy with which we can work.

Addition and Decomposition Reactions

Addition (synthesis) reactionDecomposition reaction
Two or more things join and make one compoundOne compound breaks and makes two or more things
2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl2H2O → 2H2 + O2
C + O2 → CO22KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2
Hydrogen and oxygen joining to make water: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2OCarbon dioxide breaking into carbon and oxygen is decomposition, not synthesis

mcqs.q: An exothermic process is one in which ___.
mcqs.why: In an exothermic process heat comes out, like the burning of fuel and breathing: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O + heat.

mcqs.q: An endothermic process is one in which ___.
mcqs.why: In an endothermic process heat is absorbed, like the decomposition of mercury oxide: 2HgO + heat → 2Hg + O2, and photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: Photosynthesis is an example of an ___ process.
mcqs.why: Photosynthesis absorbs energy (sunlight/heat) to make glucose, so it is an endothermic process.

mcqs.q: A synthesis (addition) reaction is an example of ___.
options: Carbon dioxide breaking into carbon and oxygen
Hydrogen and oxygen joining to make water
Water breaking into hydrogen and oxygen
mcqs.why: In a synthesis reaction, two or more things join and make one new compound: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. Hydrogen and oxygen joining to make water is the example.

mcqs.q: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2 is an example of a ___ reaction.
mcqs.why: One compound (potassium chlorate) breaks and makes two things (potassium chloride and oxygen), so it is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.q: C + O2 → CO2 is an example of a ___ reaction.
mcqs.why: Two things (carbon and oxygen) join and make one compound (carbon dioxide), so it is an addition reaction.

mcqs.q: The importance of exothermic processes is that they ___.
options: Give us heat and energy for cooking, warming houses, running engines and body work
mcqs.why: Exothermic processes give us heat and energy: burning of fuel gives heat for cooking food, warming houses and running engines, and from respiration the body gets energy to work.

mcqs.q: Breathing (respiration) is an ___ process.
mcqs.why: Breathing (respiration) is exothermic: it releases energy, and from this energy the body can work — like the burning of fuel releases heat.

mcqs.q: In a decomposition reaction, ___.
options: One compound breaks into two or more things
mcqs.why: In a decomposition reaction one compound breaks and makes two or more things, like 2H2O → 2H2 + O2.

mcqs.q: The decomposition of mercury oxide is written as ___.
mcqs.why: 2HgO + heat → 2Hg + O2. Heat is written on the left side because this decomposition absorbs heat — it is endothermic.

lessons.title: Indicators and the pH Scale
lessons.notes_html:
Indicators — Testing Acids and Bases

Indicators are substances that change colour in acids and bases, so we can identify them. Litmus paper is the most useful for testing an acidic or basic thing: it turns red in acid and blue in base.

IndicatorIn acid (HCl)In base (NaOH)In salt (NaCl)
PhenolphthaleinStays colourlessTurns pinkStays colourless
Methyl orangeOrangeYellow—
LitmusRedBlueNo change (neutral)

Activity from the book: three unlabelled beakers contain HCl, NaOH and NaCl. The beaker in which phenolphthalein turns pink is NaOH; the one in which methyl orange turns orange is HCl; the remaining neutral salt is NaCl.

The pH of Some Things

ThingpHNature
Orange juice4Acidic (most acidic of the four)
Milk6.5Slightly acidic (a little less than 7)
Blood7.3Near neutral (nearest to 7)
Ammonia11Most basic (highest pH)

Order from less to more acidic (pH from large to small): ammonia (11), blood (7.3), milk (6.5), orange juice (4).

mcqs.q: Phenolphthalein turns pink in ___.
mcqs.why: Phenolphthalein stays colourless in acid and in salt, but turns pink in a base. So the beaker in which it turns pink contains NaOH.

mcqs.q: Litmus paper turns ___ in an acid and ___ in a base.
mcqs.why: Litmus turns red in acid and blue in base. That is why litmus paper is most useful for testing whether a thing is acidic or basic.

mcqs.q: Methyl orange is ___ in acid and ___ in base.
mcqs.why: Methyl orange is orange in acid and yellow in base. Together with phenolphthalein, it helps identify the unlabelled beakers of HCl, NaOH and NaCl.

mcqs.q: The pH of milk is 6.5, so milk is ___.
mcqs.why: The pH of milk is 6.5, which is a little less than 7 (neutral), so milk is slightly acidic.

mcqs.q: Which list is in order from less to more acidic?
mcqs.why: From less to more acidic, the pH goes from large to small: ammonia 11, blood 7.3, milk 6.5, orange juice 4. Orange juice is the most acidic of the four.

mcqs.q: Which thing is the most basic?
mcqs.why: The pH of ammonia is 11, which is the highest of the four, so ammonia is the most basic.

mcqs.q: Which thing's pH is near neutral?
mcqs.why: The pH of blood is 7.3, which is nearest to the neutral value 7. Milk (6.5) is slightly acidic and ammonia (11) is basic.

mcqs.q: Which can be most useful for testing an acidic or basic thing?
mcqs.why: Litmus paper turns red in acid and blue in base, so an acidic or basic thing can be tested with it. A thermometer measures temperature, not acidity.

mcqs.q: In the book's activity, the beaker in which phenolphthalein turns pink contains ___.
mcqs.why: Phenolphthalein turns pink only in a base, so that beaker contains NaOH. The beaker where methyl orange turns orange is HCl, and the remaining neutral salt is NaCl.

mcqs.q: Orange juice has pH 4. This shows that orange juice is ___.
options: Acidic — the most acidic of blood, milk, ammonia and orange juice
mcqs.why: A pH of 4 is well below 7, so orange juice is acidic. Among blood (7.3), milk (6.5), ammonia (11) and orange juice (4), it is the most acidic.

lessons.title: Force and Pressure
lessons.notes_html:
Force

A force has both magnitude and direction.

Pressure

Pressure = force ÷ area. The international (SI) unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), also written as newtons per square metre (N/m²).

  • Pressure increases when the area of the surface decreases (with the same force).
  • Example from the book: a rectangular piece of wood placed in three ways — the pressure is greatest when the side touching the table is the smallest.

Worked Examples (from the book)

  • Aquarium: weight of water = 10000 N, bottom area = 1.6 m². Pressure = 10000 ÷ 1.6 = 6250 Pa.
  • Palm: pressure 101200 Pa, area 0.006 m². Force = pressure × area = 101200 × 0.006 = 607 N.
  • A force of 300 N produces a pressure of 4 N/m². Area = force ÷ pressure = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 m².

mcqs.q: Force has ___.
mcqs.why: Force has both magnitude and direction. Both are needed to describe a force completely.

mcqs.q: The unit of pressure in the international standard is the ___.
mcqs.why: The international unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa). Pressure is force divided by area, so it is also written as newtons per square metre.

mcqs.q: Pressure increases when ___.
options: The area of the surface increases
The magnitude of the force decreases
The area of the surface decreases
The area stays the same and force decreases
mcqs.why: Pressure = force ÷ area, so when the area decreases, the pressure increases. A piece of wood presses most where its smallest side touches the table.

mcqs.q: A large aquarium has water weighing 10000 N and a bottom area of 1.6 m². The pressure on the bottom is ___.
mcqs.why: Pressure = force ÷ area = 10000 ÷ 1.6 = 6250 pascals.

mcqs.q: If the pressure is 101200 Pa and the area of your palm is 0.006 m², the force on your hand is about ___.
mcqs.why: Force = pressure × area = 101200 × 0.006 = 607.2 ≈ 607 newtons. The air presses on our hand with this large force all the time.

mcqs.q: A force of 300 N produces a pressure of 4 N/m². The area is ___.
mcqs.why: Area = force ÷ pressure = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 square metres.

mcqs.q: A force of 46 N is applied on a piston of area 0.5 m². The pressure inside the cylinder is ___.
mcqs.why: Pressure = force ÷ area = 46 ÷ 0.5 = 92 newtons per square metre.

mcqs.q: The formula for pressure is ___.
mcqs.why: Pressure = force ÷ area. That is why the same force on a smaller area produces greater pressure.

mcqs.q: A rectangular piece of wood is placed on a table in three ways. Its pressure on the table is greatest when ___.
options: The largest side touches the table
It stands on its longest edge only
The side touching the table is the smallest
The pressure stays the same in all three ways
mcqs.why: At the position where the side of the piece of wood touching the table is the smallest, the area is least, so with the same weight the pressure becomes the greatest.

mcqs.q: Pressure is measured in pascals, which is the same as ___.
mcqs.why: One pascal is one newton per square metre (N/m²), because pressure is force (newtons) divided by area (square metres).

lessons.title: Pressure in Liquids and Pascal's Law
lessons.notes_html:
Pressure in Liquids

  • The pressure in water increases with depth — the deeper we go, the more the pressure.
  • Pascal's law: the pressure applied on a closed liquid is transferred equally to every part of the liquid and to the walls of the container. That is why we say pressure in water is transferred equally.
  • In a hydraulic power system, any incompressible liquid is used — a liquid which does not compress on being pressed; generally oil.

Use of Pascal's Law

Example: the braking system of a car and the hydraulic jack — the small force applied on the brake pedal changes through the liquid into a large force which can stop the car or lift a heavy thing up.

mcqs.q: Pressure in water is transferred equally. This rule is called ___.
mcqs.why: According to Pascal's law, the pressure applied on a liquid is transferred equally in all directions to every part of the liquid and the walls of the container.

mcqs.q: The quantity of pressure in water increases because of ___.
mcqs.why: The deeper we go in water, the more the pressure increases — that is, pressure in a liquid increases with depth.

mcqs.q: Which liquid is used in a hydraulic power system?
mcqs.why: In a hydraulic system, a liquid is used which does not compress on being pressed — generally oil. Any incompressible liquid can be used.

mcqs.q: Pascal's law states that pressure applied on a closed liquid is ___.
options: Transferred equally to every part of the liquid and the walls of the container
mcqs.why: Pascal's law: the pressure applied on a closed liquid is transferred equally to every part of the liquid and to the walls of the container. This is the working rule of hydraulic machines.

mcqs.q: An example of the use of Pascal's law is ___.
options: The braking system of a car and the hydraulic jack
mcqs.why: In a car's brakes and a hydraulic jack, a small force applied on the pedal or handle changes through the liquid into a large force which stops the car or lifts a heavy thing.

mcqs.q: In a hydraulic jack, a small force can lift a heavy load because ___.
options: The pressure is transferred equally through the liquid to a larger area
mcqs.why: The pressure applied on the closed liquid is transferred equally; acting on a larger piston area it produces a larger force, which lifts the heavy load.

mcqs.q: As we go deeper in a swimming pool, the pressure on our body ___.
mcqs.why: Pressure in water increases with depth. The deeper we go, the more water is above us pressing down, so the pressure increases.

mcqs.q: Why is oil generally used in hydraulic systems?
options: It does not compress on being pressed
mcqs.why: A hydraulic system needs a liquid which does not compress on being pressed, so that the pressure is transferred fully. Generally oil is used for this.

mcqs.q: Pressure in a closed liquid is transferred ___.
mcqs.why: Pascal's law says the pressure is transferred equally in all directions — to every part of the liquid and to the walls of the container.

mcqs.q: If pressure is applied at one point of a closed liquid, the walls of the container ___.
options: Feel the same pressure as every other part
mcqs.why: The pressure applied on a closed liquid reaches the walls of the container equally, just as it reaches every part of the liquid. This is Pascal's law.

lessons.title: Atmospheric Pressure, Gas Pressure and Aerosols
lessons.notes_html:
Atmospheric Pressure

  • Atmospheric pressure is measured by the height of the mercury column in a mercury barometer.
  • In the book's barometer picture, the mercury column is 75 cm high, so the atmospheric pressure is equal to 75 cm of mercury.
  • At a height above or below sea level, inner discomfort is felt because the pressure of our body adjusts slowly to a sudden change of outside pressure.

Pressure in a Gas

Pressure in a gas is produced by its molecules colliding with the walls of the closed container.

Aerosols

Aerosols are very small particles (liquid or solid) floating in air or gas, like the spray coming out of a spray can.

  • Working: in an aerosol can, liquid and gas under pressure are closed. When the valve is pressed, the gas pushes the liquid out of the nozzle, and the liquid comes out in the form of very small particles (spray).
  • Examples: hair spray, perfume spray, insect-killing spray, paint spray, the breathing inhaler (medicine for asthma), and the spray that spreads fragrance in a room.

Project — a Simple Barometer

Fill a glass bottle with water; fix a straight tube on the mouth with tape so its lower end dips in the water. Fix a paper scale in front of the tube. When the pressure of the air increases, the level of the water in the tube goes down; when the pressure decreases, the level goes up.

mcqs.q: Atmospheric pressure can be measured by ___.
options: The height of the water column in a barometer
The height of the lime water in a barometer
The height of oil in a barometer
The height of the mercury column in a barometer
mcqs.why: Atmospheric pressure is measured by the height of the mercury column in a mercury barometer, because mercury is a very heavy liquid.

mcqs.q: In the book's barometer picture, the mercury column is 75 cm high. The atmospheric pressure is ___.
mcqs.why: The height of the mercury column is 75 cm, so the atmospheric pressure is equal to 75 cm of mercury. The column height shows the pressure directly.

mcqs.q: At a height above or below sea level, inner discomfort is felt because ___.
options: The pressure of our body adjusts slowly
The pressure of our body stays the same
The pressure of our body adjusts quickly
mcqs.why: On a sudden change of outside pressure, the pressure of the body adjusts slowly, so discomfort is felt — for example in the ears during a fast climb.

mcqs.q: Pressure in a gas is because of ___.
options: Molecules colliding with the walls of the closed container
Molecules colliding at the bottom only
Molecules colliding with each other only
mcqs.why: The molecules of a gas keep moving and collide with the walls of the container. Pressure is produced by these collisions.

mcqs.q: Aerosols are ___.
options: Very small particles (liquid or solid) floating in air or gas
mcqs.why: Aerosols are very small particles (liquid or solid) floating in air or gas, like the spray coming out of a spray can.

mcqs.q: In an aerosol can, when the valve is pressed, ___.
options: The can becomes empty of gas first
The liquid turns into a solid
The gas under pressure pushes the liquid out of the nozzle as a fine spray
mcqs.why: In an aerosol can, liquid and gas under pressure are closed. When the valve is pressed, the gas pushes the liquid out of the nozzle, and the liquid comes out in the form of very small particles (spray).

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of an aerosol?
mcqs.why: Hair spray is an aerosol. Other examples: perfume spray, insect-killing spray, paint spray, the breathing inhaler for asthma, and room fragrance spray.

mcqs.q: The breathing inhaler used by asthma patients works as an aerosol because ___.
options: It sends the medicine out as very small particles floating in gas
It dissolves the medicine in water
mcqs.why: The inhaler is an aerosol: the medicine comes out of the pressurised can as very small particles (spray) which the patient breathes in.

mcqs.q: In the simple barometer project, when the air pressure increases, the water level in the tube ___.
mcqs.why: When the pressure of the air increases, it presses the water more and the level of the water in the tube goes down; when the pressure decreases, the level goes up.

mcqs.q: A barometer is an instrument used to find ___.
mcqs.why: A barometer finds atmospheric pressure. The mercury barometer shows it by the height of the mercury column.

lessons.title: Physical Quantities and SI Units
lessons.notes_html:
Physical Quantities

  • A quantity which can be measured is called a physical quantity, like length, mass and time.
  • A physical quantity is made of two parts: (1) the numerical value (example: 3) and (2) the unit (example: metre). In a length of 3 metres, 3 is the numerical value and metre is the unit.
  • When a standard is fixed for a quantity, that standard quantity is called a unit.

The Seven Base Units (SI)

Base physical quantityName of unitSymbol
Lengthmetrem
Masskilogramkg
Timeseconds
Electric currentampereA
TemperaturekelvinK
Amount of substancemolemol
Luminous intensitycandelacd

Newton, watt and joule are derived units, not base units. The cubic metre (m³) is the unit of volume.

What is a Prefix?

A prefix is the word or symbol placed before a unit which shows a large or small part of the unit, like kilo (1000) and milli (1/1000). A prefix can be changed back by multiplying or dividing by its numerical value: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres; 1 millimetre = 1/1000 metre.

mcqs.q: A quantity which can be measured is called a ___ quantity.
mcqs.why: A quantity which can be measured is called a physical quantity, like length, mass and time. It always has a numerical value and a unit.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a base unit?
mcqs.why: The second is the base unit of time. Newton, watt and joule are derived units, made from the base units.

mcqs.q: When a standard is fixed for a quantity, that standard quantity is called a ___.
mcqs.why: The standard quantity fixed for measurement is called a unit — for example the metre is the unit of length.

mcqs.q: A physical quantity is made of which two parts?
mcqs.why: A physical quantity is made of (1) the numerical value and (2) the unit. In '3 metres', 3 is the numerical value and metre is the unit.

mcqs.q: How many base units are there in the international system?
mcqs.why: There are seven base units: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.

mcqs.q: The unit of electric current in the international system is the ___.
mcqs.why: In the international system (SI), the unit of electric current is the ampere (A). It is one of the seven base units.

mcqs.q: The cubic metre (m³) is the unit of ___.
mcqs.why: The cubic metre (m³) is the unit of volume. Length is measured in metres and area in square metres.

mcqs.q: The base unit of temperature is the ___.
mcqs.why: The base unit of temperature in SI is the kelvin (K). The other base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, mole and candela.

mcqs.q: The symbol of the unit of luminous intensity (candela) is ___.
mcqs.why: Luminous intensity is measured in candela, symbol cd. The mole (mol) measures the amount of substance.

mcqs.q: A prefix is ___.
options: The word or symbol placed before a unit showing a large or small part of it
The end part of a scale
mcqs.why: A prefix is placed before a unit and shows a large or small part of the unit, like kilo (1000) and milli (1/1000).

mcqs.q: 1 kilometre is equal to ___.
mcqs.why: The prefix kilo means 1000, so 1 kilometre = 1000 metres. Prefixes are changed back by multiplying or dividing by their numerical value.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: Length is measured in metres (m). Mass is measured in kilograms (kg), time in seconds (s) and temperature in kelvins (K).

mcqs.q: The unit of amount of substance is the ___.
mcqs.why: The amount of substance is measured in moles (mol). It is one of the seven base quantities of the SI system.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a derived unit?
mcqs.why: The newton is a derived unit, made from the base units. Metre, kilogram and second are base units.

mcqs.q: In 'a mass of 5 kilograms', the unit is ___ and the numerical value is ___.
mcqs.why: In every measurement, the number is the numerical value and the standard quantity is the unit. Here the numerical value is 5 and the unit is kilogram.

lessons.title: Prefixes, Conversions and Measuring Instruments
lessons.notes_html:
Prefixes and Conversions

  • Increasing order for length: millimetre, centimetre, metre (and kilometre is larger still).
  • 1 kilogram = 1000 grams, so 4 kilograms = 4000 grams.
  • 1 kilometre = 1000 metres, so 0.05 kilometres = 0.05 × 1000 = 50 metres.
  • 10−3 seconds is called a millisecond (10−3 = milli). A microsecond is 10−6 s and a nanosecond is 10−9 s.

Measuring the Volume of a Liquid

A measuring cylinder (graduated cylinder) is used in the laboratory for the measurement of a liquid (its volume). The measurement is correct when:

  • The cylinder is kept on a level surface.
  • The reading is taken with the eye level with the surface (meniscus) of the liquid.
  • The lower meniscus (lower curve) is read.
  • The correct scale and correct mark of the cylinder are used.

Measuring Small Lengths

From the book: five spheres placed on a measuring strip spread from 4 cm to 16 cm, so the total length of the five spheres = 16 − 4 = 12 cm. The diameter of one sphere = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm. Measuring several objects together and dividing is an accurate way to measure one small object.

mcqs.q: What is the correct increasing order for measuring length?
mcqs.why: Increasing order: millimetre (the smallest), centimetre, metre (the largest of the three). A kilometre is even larger than a metre.

mcqs.q: A mass of 4 kilograms is equal to ___.
mcqs.why: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams, so 4 kilograms = 4 × 1000 = 4000 grams.

mcqs.q: A distance of 0.05 kilometres is equal to ___.
mcqs.why: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres, so 0.05 kilometres = 0.05 × 1000 = 50 metres.

mcqs.q: 10⁻³ seconds is called a ___.
mcqs.why: 10⁻³ = milli, so 10⁻³ seconds = 1 millisecond. A microsecond is 10⁻⁶ seconds and a nanosecond is 10⁻⁹ seconds.

mcqs.q: A measuring cylinder is used in the laboratory for ___.
mcqs.why: A measuring cylinder is used in the laboratory to measure a liquid — that is, the volume of a liquid.

mcqs.q: To read a graduated cylinder correctly, the eye should be ___.
options: Level with the surface (meniscus) of the liquid
mcqs.why: The measurement is correct when the cylinder is on a level surface and the eye is level with the meniscus of the liquid, reading the lower meniscus on the correct scale.

mcqs.q: Which meniscus is read in a measuring cylinder?
mcqs.why: The lower meniscus (lower curve) of the liquid is read. The cylinder must be on a level surface and the eye level with the liquid surface.

mcqs.q: Five spheres spread from 4 cm to 16 cm on a strip. The diameter of one sphere is ___.
mcqs.why: The total length of the five spheres = 16 − 4 = 12 cm. The diameter of one sphere = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm.

mcqs.q: 1 millimetre is equal to ___ of a metre.
mcqs.why: The prefix milli means 1/1000, so 1 millimetre = 1/1000 metre. Prefixes can be changed back by multiplying or dividing by their numerical value.

mcqs.q: Why are five spheres measured together instead of one?
options: To measure one small diameter more accurately by dividing the total
Because one sphere cannot be measured at all in any way
mcqs.why: Measuring several spheres together and dividing the total length by their number gives the diameter of one sphere more accurately than measuring a single small sphere.

chapters.title: Unit 9: Sources and Effects of Heat Energy

lessons.title: Thermal Expansion of Solids, Liquids and Gases
lessons.notes_html:
Thermal Expansion

Thermal expansion is the process in which a thing expands (becomes bigger) on being heated. On cooling, things contract (shrink).

  • Solids: heat a metal ball — it expands and does not pass through the ring; on cooling it shrinks and passes through again. A heated metal wire also becomes longer.
  • Liquids: mercury in a thermometer expands uniformly on heating and rises — that is how temperature is measured.
  • Gases expand the most on the same increase of temperature: gases (air) expand more than liquids, and liquids more than solids.

Experiment — Gases Expand on Heating

Fix a balloon on the mouth of an empty bottle and keep the bottle in hot water — the air inside becomes hot, expands and inflates the balloon. Keep the bottle in cold water and the air contracts and the balloon sits down. This proves gases expand on heating and contract on cooling.

Why Mercury is Used in a Thermometer

  • It expands uniformly with heat.
  • It does not stick to glass.
  • It takes the temperature quickly.
  • It is clearly visible because it is shiny.

Where Expansion and Contraction are Used

  • Bimetallic strip — two different metals joined together; used in the electric iron as a thermostat.
  • Riveting — used to join a hard thing with a hard thing (two hard metal plates) firmly.
  • Expansion and contraction are NOT used in an electric fan.

mcqs.q: Thermal expansion is ___.
options: The shrinking of a thing on heating
The process in which a thing expands on being heated
mcqs.why: Thermal expansion is the process in which a thing expands (becomes bigger) on being heated. On cooling, the same thing contracts (shrinks) back.

mcqs.q: After heating, an iron ball does not pass through the ring because ___.
options: The ball expands and becomes bigger on heating
mcqs.why: On heating, the iron ball expands and becomes bigger, so it does not pass through the hole of the ring. On cooling, it shrinks and passes through again — this shows the expansion of solids.

mcqs.q: The balloon on a bottle kept in hot water inflates because ___.
options: The balloon is made of rubber
The air inside the bottle heats and expands
mcqs.why: The air inside the bottle becomes hot and expands, and its extra volume inflates the balloon. In cold water the air contracts and the balloon sits down — gases expand on heating and contract on cooling.

mcqs.q: Which of the following expands the most on the same increase of temperature?
mcqs.why: On the same increase of temperature, gases (air) expand the most, after that liquids, and then solids expand the least.

mcqs.q: Which liquid is used in a thermometer?
mcqs.why: Mercury is used in a thermometer because it expands uniformly on heating and is clearly visible.

mcqs.q: Mercury is used in a thermometer because it ___.
options: Expands uniformly, does not stick to glass, takes temperature quickly and is shiny and visible
mcqs.why: Mercury expands uniformly with heat, does not stick to glass, takes the temperature quickly, and is clearly visible because it is shiny.

mcqs.q: A bimetallic strip is used in a/an ___.
mcqs.why: In an electric iron, a bimetallic strip is used as a thermostat which keeps the temperature under control by bending and breaking the circuit.

mcqs.q: Riveting is used to join ___.
options: A hard thing with a hard thing
A soft thing with a hard thing
A soft thing with a soft thing
mcqs.why: By riveting, two hard metal plates are joined firmly — a hard thing with a hard thing. The hot rivet expands and then contracts to hold the plates tightly.

mcqs.q: In which of the following is expansion and contraction NOT used?
mcqs.why: Expansion and contraction are not used in an electric fan. In the iron a thermostat (bimetallic strip), in the railway track expansion gaps, and in the thermometer the expansion of mercury are used.

mcqs.q: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because ___.
options: The two metals expand by different amounts
mcqs.why: A bimetallic strip is made of strips of two different metals which expand by different amounts on heating. The strip bends because one side expands more than the other.

mcqs.q: On cooling, a heated metal wire ___.
mcqs.why: Metals expand on heating and contract on cooling. The heated wire becomes longer in heat and shrinks back on cooling.

mcqs.q: The two-walled thermometer of the book uses which liquid?
mcqs.why: Mercury is the liquid used in the thermometer described in the book, because it expands uniformly and is clearly visible.

mcqs.q: The expansion of a gas can be shown by ___.
options: A balloon on a bottle in hot water
mcqs.why: Fix a balloon on the mouth of an empty bottle in hot water: the air expands and inflates the balloon. In cold water it contracts and the balloon sits down.

mcqs.q: A thermostat in an electric iron works with the help of ___.
mcqs.why: The bimetallic strip in electric parts bends on heating because its two metals expand differently, so the electric circuit is automatically closed or opened — the work of a thermostat.

mcqs.q: Liquids expand ___ solids on the same increase of temperature.
mcqs.why: On the same increase of temperature, gases expand the most, liquids expand more than solids, and solids expand the least.

lessons.title: Effects of Expansion and the Anomalous Expansion of Water
lessons.notes_html:
Harmful Effects of Expansion and Contraction — and How to Reduce Them

  • In heat, railway tracks expand and can bend — a danger of a railway accident. Gaps are left in railway tracks to give room for expansion.
  • The parts of bridges expand and increase pressure, and the bridge can be harmed. Expansion joints are fitted in bridges.
  • Crack control joints are made in roads.
  • Telephone wires expand in the heat of summer, become longer, and so hang down between the poles.
