The Anomalous (Strange) Expansion of Water

  • The strange characteristic of water is that on cooling below 4 degrees, water expands instead of shrinking, and it expands even more on becoming ice.
  • Ice, being lighter than water, floats on top. So in winter the water under the surface of a pond stays liquid and aquatic life stays alive.
  • Because water expands on freezing, the volume of ice is more than that of water — the pressure on the walls of a pipe increases and pipes burst in the cold.

How a Bimetallic Strip Works

A bimetallic strip is made of strips of two different metals. On heating, one metal expands more and the strip bends; this bending drives the measurement of temperature or works an electric switch (thermostat) — for example in an electric iron.

mcqs.q: Why is a gap left in railway tracks?
options: Because the tracks expand in the heat of summer and need room
For the sound of the train
mcqs.why: In the heat of summer, railway tracks expand. If a gap were not left, the tracks would bend and an accident could happen; the gap gives room for expansion.

mcqs.q: Telephone wires hang down during summer days because ___.
options: The metal wires expand in heat and become longer
The wires become heavy with rain
mcqs.why: In heat, the metal wires expand and become longer, so they hang down between two poles. In winter they contract and become tight.

mcqs.q: What problems occur in bridges because of thermal expansion?
options: The parts expand, pressure increases and the bridge can be harmed — so expansion joints are left
mcqs.why: The parts of bridges expand in heat and increase pressure, and the bridge can be harmed. For this, gaps and expansion joints are left in bridges, as in railway tracks.

mcqs.q: The strange characteristic of water on freezing is that it ___.
mcqs.why: Unlike ordinary things, water expands on freezing, and it starts expanding even on cooling below 4 degrees. So ice, being lighter, floats on top of water.

mcqs.q: Because of the anomalous expansion of water, in winter ___.
options: Ice floats on top and the water below stays liquid, so aquatic life stays alive
mcqs.why: Ice, being lighter than water, floats on top, so in winter the water under the surface of a pond stays liquid and aquatic life stays alive under the ice.

mcqs.q: When water freezes in pipes, the pipes burst because ___.
options: Water expands on freezing and the pressure on the pipe walls increases
mcqs.why: Water expands on freezing and the volume of ice becomes more than that of water, so the pressure on the walls of the pipe increases and the pipe bursts.

mcqs.q: Water starts expanding on cooling below ___ degrees.
mcqs.why: Water, on cooling below 4 degrees, expands instead of shrinking — this is its anomalous (strange) expansion. It expands even more on becoming ice.

mcqs.q: The harmful effects of expansion in metals can be reduced by ___.
options: Leaving gaps in tracks, fitting expansion joints in bridges and making crack control joints in roads
mcqs.why: Metals expand in heat and contract in cold, which can bend tracks and break bridges and roads. Leaving gaps, fitting expansion joints and making crack control joints reduce these harmful effects.

mcqs.q: How does a bimetallic strip work in a thermometer or thermostat?
options: Its two metals expand by different amounts, so it bends and drives the measurement or switch
It melts at a fixed temperature
mcqs.why: A bimetallic strip is made of two different metals which expand by different amounts on heating. On heating, the strip bends; this bending drives the measurement of temperature or an electric switch (thermostat).

mcqs.q: Railway tracks can bend in heat, which creates a danger of ___.
mcqs.why: In heat, railway tracks expand and bend, and there is a danger of a railway accident. Gaps left between the rails give room for this expansion.

lessons.title: Lenses — Parts and Types
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a Lens

  • Principal axis — the horizontal straight line passing through the middle of a lens.
  • Optical centre (O) — the point through which a ray of light passes without changing its path.
  • Focal point (F) — the point where rays meet (or appear to meet) after passing through the lens.
  • Focal length — the distance between the optical centre of the lens and the focal point.

Convex and Concave Lenses

Convex lensConcave lens
Thick in the middle, thin at the edgesThin in the middle, thick at the edges
Converges (joins) raysSpreads (diverges) rays
Forms both real and virtual imagesAlways forms a virtual, erect and diminished image
Used in a magnifying glass and a cameraUsed in spectacles for short sightedness and in a door peep hole

Similarities: both are lenses, both are transparent, both bend light (refraction), and both have an optical centre, a principal axis and a focal point.

Thickness and Focal Length

The thicker (more curved) the lens is, the more it bends the rays and the shorter its focal length becomes. The thinner the lens, the longer its focal length.

Parallel Rays from Infinity

When the object is at infinity, the rays are parallel and, passing through a convex lens, they meet at the focal point.

mcqs.q: A horizontal line which passes through a lens is called the ___.
mcqs.why: The straight line passing through the middle of a lens is called the principal axis. The optical centre is a point on this line.

mcqs.q: The point through which a ray of light passes without changing its path is the ___.
mcqs.why: A ray passing through the optical centre of the lens goes straight without changing its path. This is one of the three standard rays used in ray diagrams.

mcqs.q: The distance between the optical centre of the lens and the focal point is called the ___.
mcqs.why: The distance between the optical centre and the focal point is called the focal length. A thicker lens has a shorter focal length.

mcqs.q: When the object is at infinity, parallel rays pass through a ___ lens and meet at the focal point.
mcqs.why: The parallel rays coming from infinity pass through a convex lens and meet at the focal point (F), because a convex lens converges rays.

mcqs.q: A convex lens is ___.
options: Thin in the middle and thick at the edges
Thick in the middle and thin at the edges
mcqs.why: A convex lens is thick in the middle and thin at the edges, and it converges rays. A concave lens is thin in the middle and thick at the edges, and it spreads rays.

mcqs.q: How does the thickness of a lens affect its focal length?
options: A thicker lens has a longer focal length
A thicker lens bends rays more and its focal length becomes shorter
A thinner lens has a shorter focal length
mcqs.why: The thicker (more curved) the lens is, the more it bends the rays and the shorter its focal length becomes. The thinner the lens, the longer its focal length.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a similarity between convex and concave lenses?
options: Both are transparent and bend light (refraction)
Both are thick in the middle
mcqs.why: Both lenses are transparent, both bend light (refraction), and both have an optical centre, a principal axis and a focal point. They differ in shape and in the images they form.

mcqs.q: A concave lens is used in ___.
options: Spectacles for short sightedness and a door peep hole
mcqs.why: A concave lens is used in spectacles for short sightedness and in a door peep hole. A convex lens is used in a magnifying glass and a camera.

mcqs.q: A ray parallel to the principal axis, after passing through a convex lens, ___.
mcqs.why: In a convex lens, a ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the lens and goes through the focal point (F). This is the first rule of the ray diagram.

mcqs.q: The optical centre of a lens is marked by the letter ___.
mcqs.why: The optical centre is marked O and the focal point is marked F. The distance OF is the focal length of the lens.

lessons.title: Images Formed by Lenses
lessons.notes_html:
Image Formation by a Convex Lens

The three rules of the ray diagram:

  • A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the lens and goes through the focal point (F).
  • A ray passing through the optical centre (O) goes straight.
  • A ray passing through the focal point becomes parallel to the axis after the lens.

The image is formed where these rays meet.

Image Formation by a Concave Lens

Through a concave lens, the rays spread out and meet on being extended backwards. So the image is always virtual, erect and smaller than the original object, and it is formed on the same side of the lens on which the object is. An erect, diminished image is formed when the object is placed at any distance in front of a concave lens.

Uses

  • A convex lens is used as a magnifying glass to show things enlarged.
  • In a camera, to obtain a clear image, the lens is moved forward and backward to correct the focus.

mcqs.q: A ___ lens is used as a magnifying glass to show things enlarged.
mcqs.why: A convex lens shows things enlarged, so it is used as a magnifying glass. It converges the rays coming from a near object.

mcqs.q: The image formed by a concave lens is always ___.
options: Inverted and of the same size
mcqs.why: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished (smaller) image, wherever the object is placed. The rays spread out and only appear to meet.

mcqs.q: An erect, diminished image is formed when the object is placed at ___ in front of a concave lens.
mcqs.why: At any distance — a concave lens always forms an erect, virtual and diminished image, at whatever distance the object is placed in front of it.

mcqs.q: In a ray diagram of a convex lens, a ray passing through the optical centre ___.
mcqs.why: A ray passing through the optical centre (O) goes straight without changing its path. Together with the parallel ray and the focal ray, it locates the image.

mcqs.q: A ray passing through the focal point of a convex lens becomes ___ after the lens.
mcqs.why: A ray passing through the focal point becomes parallel to the axis after passing through a convex lens. This is the third rule of the ray diagram.

mcqs.q: To obtain a clear image in a camera, ___.
options: The film is moved forward and backward
The lens is moved forward and backward
Both lens and film are moved
mcqs.why: In a camera, the lens is moved forward and backward to correct the focus so that a clear image is obtained on the film.

mcqs.q: Through a concave lens, the image is formed ___.
options: On the same side of the lens as the object
mcqs.why: Through a concave lens the rays spread out and meet on being extended backwards, so the virtual image is formed on the same side of the lens on which the object is.

mcqs.q: The image in a convex lens is formed where ___.
mcqs.why: The image is formed where the rays meet after passing through the lens — the parallel ray through F, the central ray straight, and the focal ray becoming parallel locate that point.

mcqs.q: A magnifying glass enlarges things because it uses a ___ lens.
mcqs.why: A convex lens is used as a magnifying glass to show things enlarged. Placed near an object, it forms an erect, enlarged, virtual image.

mcqs.q: Which image can be obtained on a screen?
options: A real image formed by a convex lens
The virtual image of a concave lens
The image in a peep hole
mcqs.why: A real image, formed where rays actually meet through a convex lens, can be obtained on a screen. A concave lens forms only virtual images, which cannot be caught on a screen.

lessons.title: The Human Eye and Its Defects
lessons.notes_html:
The Eye and the Camera

Part of the cameraSame part of the eyeSame work
AperturePupil / irisControlling the quantity of light
LensLens of the eyeFocusing the light and making the image
FilmRetinaObtaining and sensing the image
  • A convex lens is present in the human eye; it focuses the light and makes an image on the retina.
  • The ciliary muscles change the shape (form) of the lens of the eye and correct the focus.

Defects of the Eye

Short sightedness (myopia)Long sightedness (hypermetropia)
Distant things are not seen clearlyNear things are not seen clearly
Light focuses in front of the retinaLight focuses behind the retina; the near point moves far away
Treatment: spectacles with concave lensesTreatment: spectacles with convex lenses

In the ray diagram of short sightedness, parallel rays from a distant object focus in front of the retina, so a blurred image is formed on the retina. A concave lens spreads the rays so that they focus on the retina.

mcqs.q: Which part helps in changing the shape of the lens in the eye?
mcqs.why: The ciliary muscles change the shape and form of the lens of the eye and correct the focus, so we can see near and distant things.

mcqs.q: The type of lens present in the human eye is a ___.
mcqs.why: A convex lens is present in the eye, which focuses the light and makes an image on the retina of the eye.

mcqs.q: In short sightedness, the light of distant things focuses ___.
mcqs.why: In short sightedness (myopia), the light of distant things focuses in front of the retina and distant things are not seen clearly. A concave lens in spectacles corrects it.

mcqs.q: In long sightedness (hypermetropia), ___.
options: Distant things are not seen clearly
The near point moves very far away and light from a near object focuses behind the retina
Light focuses in front of the retina
mcqs.why: In long sightedness, the near point of the eye moves far away, so near things are not seen clearly and the light focuses behind the retina. Spectacles with convex lenses are used for treatment.

mcqs.q: Short sightedness is corrected by spectacles with ___ lenses.
mcqs.why: In short sightedness, spectacles with concave lenses are used: the concave lens spreads the rays so that they focus on the retina instead of in front of it.

mcqs.q: Long sightedness is corrected by spectacles with ___ lenses.
mcqs.why: In long sightedness, spectacles with convex lenses are used, which converge the light more so it focuses on the retina instead of behind it.

mcqs.q: The part of the eye that corresponds to the film of a camera is the ___.
mcqs.why: Film — retina of the eye — obtaining and sensing the image. The aperture corresponds to the pupil/iris, and the camera lens to the lens of the eye.

mcqs.q: The aperture of the camera and the pupil of the eye both do the work of ___.
options: Changing the shape of the lens
mcqs.why: Aperture of the camera — pupil/iris of the eye — controlling the quantity of light. Both widen or narrow to let more or less light in.

mcqs.q: The lens of the eye makes the image on the ___.
mcqs.why: The convex lens of the eye focuses the light and makes an image on the retina of the eye, just as the camera lens makes the image on the film.

mcqs.q: A person who cannot see near things clearly has ___.
mcqs.why: In long sightedness (hypermetropia), near things are not seen clearly because the near point moves far away and light focuses behind the retina.

mcqs.q: A person who cannot see distant things clearly has ___ and it is treated with ___.
mcqs.why: In short sightedness (myopia), distant things are not seen clearly and light focuses in front of the retina. Spectacles with concave lenses spread the rays onto the retina.

mcqs.q: In the ray diagram for short sightedness, a blurred image is formed on the retina because the rays focus ___.
mcqs.why: The parallel rays coming from a distant object pass through the lens of the eye and focus in front of the retina, so a blurred image is formed on the retina. A concave lens corrects this.

lessons.title: Electric Current — AC and DC
lessons.notes_html:
Electric Current

  • The flow of electrons is called electric current.
  • In a bicycle generator (dynamo), the magnet rotates to produce electricity in the coil of wire.

Direct Current and Alternating Current

Direct current (DC)Alternating current (AC)
Flows in one direction onlyIts direction changes again and again
Obtained from a cell and a batteryObtained from a generator; the mains electricity of homes and schools
Voltage cannot be changed easilyVoltage can be increased or decreased with a transformer

Basic Components of an Electric Circuit

  • The source of electricity (cell or battery).
  • Connecting wires.
  • A switch.
  • A bulb or another load (like a motor).
  • A resistor.

With these, the circuit is completed and electricity flows.

mcqs.q: The flow of electrons is called ___.
mcqs.why: The flow of electrons is called electric current. It flows in a circuit when the circuit is completed.

mcqs.q: The electricity obtained from a cell is called ___.
mcqs.why: Direct current is obtained from a cell, and it flows in one direction only. A battery also gives direct current.

mcqs.q: The electricity used in our homes and schools is ___.
mcqs.why: Alternating current is used in homes and schools; its direction keeps changing. It is obtained from generators.

mcqs.q: Which part of a bicycle generator rotates to produce electricity?
mcqs.why: In a bicycle generator, the magnet rotates, by which electricity is produced in the coil of wire.

mcqs.q: The difference between AC and DC is that ___.
options: AC flows in one direction; DC changes direction
DC is used in homes; AC in torches
DC flows in one direction only; AC changes direction again and again
mcqs.why: Direct current flows in one direction only and is obtained from a cell and battery. Alternating current changes direction again and again and is the mains electricity of homes, whose voltage can be changed with a transformer.

mcqs.q: The voltage of AC can be increased or decreased with a ___.
mcqs.why: The voltage of alternating current can be increased or decreased with a transformer. This is a big advantage of AC over DC, whose voltage cannot be changed easily.

mcqs.q: The basic components of an electric circuit are ___.
options: Source of electricity, connecting wires, switch, load (bulb/motor) and resistor
Only a cell and a switch
mcqs.why: The basic components are: the source of electricity (cell or battery), connecting wires, a switch, a bulb or another load like a motor, and a resistor. With these the circuit is completed and electricity flows.

mcqs.q: A cell and a battery are examples of ___.
mcqs.why: The cell or battery is the source of electricity in a circuit. It gives direct current (DC).

mcqs.q: Which of these is a load in a circuit?
mcqs.why: A bulb or a motor is a load — it uses the electricity. The cell is the source, wires connect the parts, and the switch opens or closes the circuit.

mcqs.q: Electricity is produced in a generator when ___.
options: A magnet rotates near a coil of wire
mcqs.why: In a bicycle generator the magnet rotates and electricity is produced in the coil of wire. Big generators in power stations work on the same idea.

lessons.title: Producing Electricity and Energy Sources
lessons.notes_html:
How Electricity is Produced in a Power Station

The stages in correct order:

  • 1. Fuel burns and heats the water tank.
  • 2. Water changes into steam under pressure.
  • 3. Steam rotates the turbines.
  • 4. Turbines turn the generators.
  • 5. Electricity is produced and is included in the national grid.

Through windmills: wind energy → wind pushes and rotates the blades → energy of the motion of the rotating blades → the blades rotate the generator and produce electricity → energy obtained from the turbine (output).

Renewable and Non-Renewable Sources

  • Renewable: wind energy, geothermal energy, wave energy, solar energy, bio-fuels.
  • Not renewable: natural gas — a finishing fossil fuel.
  • Biogas — the gas formed when the waste of animals and plants, buried in the ground in the absence of air, rots.
  • Bio-fuels are a cheap source of energy because they are made from the waste and dirt of animals and plants, which are free and found everywhere, and they are renewable — they can be obtained again and again.

Advantages of Solar Electricity

  • Sunlight is free and found everywhere.
  • It is renewable and does not finish.
  • No pollution comes from it.
  • The maintenance of solar panels is little.
  • Electricity can be reached even to far-off areas.

Problems of Power Production

  • Nuclear power generator: the radioactive waste is dangerous and difficult to keep safe, there is a danger of accident, and setting up the plant is expensive.
  • Thermal power generator: the burning of fuel produces pollution in the air and carbon dioxide, the fuel (coal, gas) is finishing, and fuel is expensive.

mcqs.q: In a power station, the correct order of stages is ___.
options: Steam first, then fuel burns, then turbines
Generators turn first, then fuel burns
Fuel burns and heats water → water changes into steam → steam rotates turbines → turbines turn generators → electricity joins the national grid
Water rotates turbines → fuel burns → steam forms
mcqs.why: First the fuel burns and heats the water tank; the water changes into steam under pressure; the steam rotates the turbines; the turbines turn the generators; and the electricity produced is included in the national grid.

mcqs.q: In a windmill, the energy changes are: wind energy → ___ → electricity.
options: Energy of motion of the rotating blades
mcqs.why: Wind pushes and rotates the blades, giving the energy of motion of the rotating blades; the blades rotate the generator and produce electricity, which is the energy obtained from the turbine.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a source of renewable energy?
mcqs.why: Natural gas is not a renewable source; it is a finishing fossil fuel. Wind, geothermal heat and waves are renewable sources.

mcqs.q: The gas formed from the waste of animals and plants buried without air is called ___.
mcqs.why: The gas formed from the waste of animals and plants in the absence of air is called biogas. It can be used as a fuel.

mcqs.q: Bio-fuels are called a cheap source of energy because ___.
options: They are made from free waste of animals and plants, found everywhere, and are renewable
mcqs.why: Bio-fuels are made from the waste and dirt of animals and plants, which are free and found everywhere, and they are renewable sources which can be obtained again and again.

mcqs.q: An advantage of solar electricity is that ___.
options: Sunlight is free, it is renewable, it makes no pollution and can reach far-off areas
It needs a lot of maintenance
mcqs.why: Sunlight is free and found everywhere; solar electricity is renewable and does not finish; no pollution comes from it; the maintenance of solar panels is little; and electricity can be reached even to far-off areas.

mcqs.q: A problem of a nuclear power generator is that ___.
options: Its radioactive waste is dangerous and difficult to keep safe
mcqs.why: In nuclear power, the radioactive waste is dangerous and difficult to keep safe, there is a danger of accident, and setting up the plant is expensive.

mcqs.q: A problem of a thermal power generator is that ___.
options: Burning fuel produces air pollution and carbon dioxide, and the fuel is finishing and expensive
mcqs.why: In a thermal power generator, the burning of fuel produces pollution in the air and carbon dioxide; the fuel (coal, gas) is finishing, and fuel is expensive.

mcqs.q: Wind energy, geothermal energy and wave energy are all ___.
mcqs.why: These are renewable sources — they do not finish. Natural gas, in contrast, is a finishing fossil fuel and is not renewable.

mcqs.q: Steam under pressure in a power station rotates the ___.
mcqs.why: The steam rotates the turbines, and the turbines turn the generators, which produce the electricity.

mcqs.q: Biogas is formed when plant and animal waste rots ___.
mcqs.why: Biogas is formed from the waste of animals and plants buried in the ground in the absence of air.

mcqs.q: Solar panels need ___ maintenance.
mcqs.why: The maintenance of solar panels is little — one of the advantages of solar electricity, along with free sunlight and no pollution.

lessons.title: Electronic Devices — Input and Output
lessons.notes_html:
Electronic Parts

  • Transistor — the electronic part which can be used as a switch or as a voltage amplifier.
  • IC — abbreviation of Integrated Circuit, in which many electronic parts are in one chip.
  • Silicon is an example of a semiconductor, so it is used in making transistors and chips.

Input and Output Parts (Devices)

Input parts — enter information or orders into a computerOutput parts — show the result outside
KeyboardMonitor
MousePrinter
Barcode readerSpeaker
Scanner
Microphone

A barcode is read by an input device (barcode reader), which enters information into a computer.

mcqs.q: The electronic part which can be used as a switch or as a voltage amplifier is the ___.
mcqs.why: A transistor can be used as a switch and as a voltage amplifier. It is a basic part of electronic circuits and chips.

mcqs.q: IC is the abbreviation of ___.
mcqs.why: IC means Integrated Circuit, in which many electronic parts are in one chip.

mcqs.q: Silicon is an example of a ___.
mcqs.why: Silicon is a semiconductor, so it is used in making transistors and chips.

mcqs.q: A barcode is read by a/an ___.
mcqs.why: A barcode reader is an input device which enters information into a computer.

mcqs.q: Input parts are those which ___.
options: Enter information or orders into a computer
mcqs.why: Input parts enter information or orders into a computer, like the keyboard, mouse, barcode reader, scanner and microphone. Output parts, like the monitor, printer and speaker, show the result outside.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an output device?
mcqs.why: The monitor is an output device — it shows the result of the computer outside. Keyboard, mouse and scanner are input devices.

mcqs.q: A microphone is an ___ device.
mcqs.why: A microphone enters sound (information) into a computer, so it is an input device. A speaker, which brings sound out, is an output device.

mcqs.q: In an integrated circuit (IC), ___.
options: Many electronic parts are in one chip
mcqs.why: An IC (Integrated Circuit) has many electronic parts — like transistors and resistors — made in one small chip.

mcqs.q: Silicon is used in making transistors and chips because it is a ___.
mcqs.why: Silicon is a semiconductor: its conduction can be controlled, which is exactly what transistors and chips need to work as switches and amplifiers.

mcqs.q: Which list contains only output parts?
mcqs.why: Monitor, printer and speaker all show the result of the computer outside, so they are output parts. Keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone and barcode reader are input parts.

lessons.title: Telescopes and the Spectroscope
lessons.notes_html:
Important Terms

  • Telescope — the instrument which shows far-away things close. The word telescope is a combination of two Greek words: "tele" (far) and "scope" (to see).
  • Reflecting telescope — the telescope which uses mirrors to reflect light; it has primary and secondary mirrors.
  • Refracting telescope — the telescope which uses lenses to bend light; it has two lenses.
  • Spectroscope — the instrument which divides light into a spectrum and identifies the chemical elements present in a star.
  • Space exploration — the process of searching space and using it.
  • Space debris — the rubbish of useless and damaged things in space, like old satellites and pieces of rockets.

The Spectroscope

  • Structure — three main parts: (1) an opaque barrier with a slit which makes a thin ray of light, (2) a prism which divides the light into its seven colours, (3) a screen or detector which records the light obtained.
  • Working: light passes through the slit and falls on the prism; the prism divides it into a spectrum of seven colours; from that spectrum the chemical elements present in a star are identified.
  • In the spectrum of white light, the wavelength of violet colour is the shortest.

mcqs.q: A spectroscope is used for ___.
options: Discovering the sound waves coming out of a star
Bending the light of a star to one point
Identifying the chemical elements present in a star
Marking the location of a star
mcqs.why: A spectroscope divides a star's light into a spectrum and from it identifies the chemical elements present in the star.

mcqs.q: A reflecting telescope consists of ___.
options: A prism for the division of light
mcqs.why: A reflecting telescope has primary and secondary mirrors which reflect the light and focus it. A refracting telescope, in contrast, uses lenses.

mcqs.q: The word 'telescope' is a combination of ___ words.
mcqs.why: Telescope is made of two Greek words: 'tele' (far) and 'scope' (to see) — the instrument which shows far-away things close.

mcqs.q: In a reflecting telescope, ___ are used.
mcqs.why: In a reflecting telescope, mirrors are used to reflect the light. In a refracting telescope, lenses are used to bend the light.

mcqs.q: The wavelength of ___ colour is the shortest in the spectrum of white light.
mcqs.why: In the spectrum (strip) of white light, the wavelength of violet colour is the shortest, and red is the longest.

mcqs.q: A telescope is an instrument which ___.
mcqs.why: A telescope shows far-away things close, which is why it is used to study the Moon, planets and stars.

mcqs.q: A refracting telescope works by using ___.
mcqs.why: A refracting telescope uses lenses to bend light and has two lenses. A reflecting telescope uses mirrors to reflect light.

mcqs.q: The three main parts of a spectroscope are ___.
options: A slit barrier, a prism and a screen or detector
A bulb, a prism and a mirror
mcqs.why: A spectroscope has: (1) an opaque barrier with a slit which makes a thin ray of light, (2) a prism which divides the light into seven colours, (3) a screen or detector which records the light obtained.

mcqs.q: In a spectroscope, the prism divides the light into ___.
mcqs.why: Light passes through the slit and falls on the prism; the prism divides it into a spectrum of seven colours, and from that spectrum the chemical elements in a star are identified.

mcqs.q: How is a reflecting telescope different from a refracting telescope?
options: The reflecting uses mirrors to reflect light; the refracting uses lenses to bend light
mcqs.why: A reflecting telescope uses mirrors (primary and secondary) to reflect light, whereas a refracting telescope uses two lenses to bend light.

mcqs.q: From the spectrum of a star's light, a spectroscope tells us ___.
options: The age of the star only
The distance of the star only
The chemical elements present in the star
The size of the star only
mcqs.why: Each element gives its own pattern in the spectrum, so the spectroscope identifies the chemical elements present in a star from the spectrum of its light.

lessons.title: Spacecraft, Satellites and GPS
lessons.notes_html:
Spacecraft and Satellites

  • A spacecraft can be with humans (manned) or without humans (unmanned).
  • According to the book, the Apollo 17 command module is the spacecraft which took humans to the Moon.
  • Technological instruments used in space exploration: telescopes, spectroscopes, spacecraft, artificial satellites, robots, telecommunication instruments, solar cells, GPS receivers and cameras.

Parts of an Artificial Satellite / Spacecraft

PartWork
Solar panelsProducing electricity from sunlight
Cameras and other devicesMaking scientific measurements and taking pictures
AntennasSending and receiving signals for contact with the earth
Micro thrustersChanging the direction and speed of the spacecraft and keeping it in the correct orbit
GPS receiverFinding the place of the spacecraft

The Global Positioning System (GPS)

  • GPS is a system of artificial satellites which tells the correct location, route and time of any place on the earth.
  • It consists of more than 30 artificial satellites (30 or more).
  • Every GPS satellite completes two orbits in 24 hours (one full orbit in half a day).

mcqs.q: According to the book, which Moon command module took humans to the Moon?
mcqs.why: According to the book, the Apollo 17 command module is the spacecraft which took humans to the Moon.

mcqs.q: The Global Positioning System (GPS) consists of how many artificial satellites?
mcqs.why: According to the book, in GPS there are 30 or more artificial satellites in orbit around the earth — more than 30.

mcqs.q: Every satellite of GPS completes ___ orbits in 24 hours.
mcqs.why: Every GPS satellite completes one full orbit in half a day, so it completes two orbits in 24 hours.

mcqs.q: A spacecraft can be ___.
mcqs.why: Spacecraft are of both kinds — manned (with humans) and unmanned (without humans). Both are used in space exploration.

mcqs.q: Solar panels on a satellite do the work of ___.
mcqs.why: Solar panels produce electricity from sunlight, which runs all the instruments of the satellite.

mcqs.q: Antennas on a spacecraft are used for ___.
options: Sending and receiving signals for contact with the earth
mcqs.why: Antennas send and receive signals for contact with the earth. Cameras take pictures and make measurements, and micro thrusters keep the craft in the correct orbit.

mcqs.q: Micro thrusters on a spacecraft are used to ___.
options: Change the direction and speed and keep the craft in the correct orbit
mcqs.why: Micro thrusters change the direction and speed of the spacecraft and keep it in the correct orbit. The GPS receiver finds the place of the spacecraft.

mcqs.q: GPS tells us ___ of any place on the earth.
options: The correct location, route and time
mcqs.why: The Global Positioning System is a system of artificial satellites which tells the correct location, route and time of any place on the earth.

mcqs.q: Which instruments are used in space exploration?
options: Telescopes, spectroscopes, spacecraft, satellites, robots, solar cells, GPS receivers and cameras
mcqs.why: Instruments used in space exploration include telescopes, spectroscopes, spacecraft, artificial satellites, robots, telecommunication instruments, solar cells, GPS receivers, cameras and other instruments.

mcqs.q: Cameras and devices on a satellite are used for ___.
options: Making scientific measurements and taking pictures
mcqs.why: Cameras and other devices make scientific measurements and take pictures — for example, pictures of the earth from a weather or observation satellite.

lessons.title: Benefits and Problems of Space Exploration
lessons.notes_html:
Benefits of Space Exploration in Health and Treatment

  • Imaging technologies like MRI and CT came from space research — according to the book, they were obtained as a result of understanding the images of the Moon.
  • MRI is the abbreviation of Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
  • The heart pump for heart patients was made from space technology.
  • The cooling suit is used to keep the body temperature of patients under control.
  • With robot technology, treatment (telemedicine) in far-off areas became possible.
  • From space research, new knowledge about medicines and the human body was obtained.

Life of an Astronaut and Problems of Space Exploration

  • The astronaut wears a special suit, lives in a space station, eats special food and works in weightlessness.
  • Problems: space debris (old satellites and pieces of rockets) is increasing, which is a danger for new satellites and spacecraft; and space missions are expensive.

mcqs.q: MRI and CT were obtained as a result of understanding the images of ___.
mcqs.why: As a result of the technology for understanding the images of the Moon, medical imaging technologies like MRI and CT were obtained.

mcqs.q: MRI is the abbreviation of ___.
mcqs.why: MRI means Magnetic Resonance Imaging. It is one of the health benefits that came from space research.

mcqs.q: Five benefits of space exploration in health include ___.
options: MRI and CT imaging, heart pump, cooling suit, telemedicine by robots, and new knowledge of medicines and the body
mcqs.why: Space research gave health: imaging technologies like MRI and CT, the heart pump for heart patients, the cooling suit for controlling body temperature, robot telemedicine for far-off areas, and new knowledge about medicines and the human body.

mcqs.q: The heart pump for heart patients was made from ___.
mcqs.why: The heart pump for heart patients was made from space technology — an example of space research helping treatment on earth.

mcqs.q: Space debris means ___.
options: The rubbish of useless and damaged things in space, like old satellites and pieces of rockets
mcqs.why: Space debris is the rubbish of useless and damaged things in space, like old satellites and pieces of rockets. It is increasing and is a danger for new satellites and spacecraft.

mcqs.q: A problem arising because of space exploration is ___.
options: Space debris increasing and space missions being expensive
mcqs.why: Space debris is increasing, which is a danger for new satellites and spacecraft, and space missions are expensive — these are the problems of space exploration given in the book.

mcqs.q: The life of an astronaut in space is such that he ___.
options: Wears a special suit, lives in a space station, eats special food and works in weightlessness
Eats ordinary food in a house
mcqs.why: The astronaut wears a special suit, lives in a space station, eats special food and works in weightlessness, because there is no air and almost no gravity effect in space.

mcqs.q: With robot technology from space research, what became possible?
mcqs.why: With robot technology, treatment (telemedicine) in far-off areas became possible — doctors can guide treatment from a distance.

mcqs.q: The cooling suit obtained from space technology is used to ___.
options: Keep the body temperature of patients under control
mcqs.why: The cooling suit is used to keep the body temperature of patients under control. It came from the suits developed for astronauts.

mcqs.q: Space exploration is the process of ___.
mcqs.why: Space exploration is the process of searching space and using it — with telescopes, spacecraft, satellites and robots — and its benefits reach health, communication and daily life on earth.
